    ## 8. Layer 3: Operational Intelligence, Analytics, Reporting & Recognition
    
    Layer 3 transforms the raw, timestamped operational data captured in Layer 2 into real-time business intelligence, automated executive reports, and performance recognition standings.
    
    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
        subgraph DataIngest["DATA INGESTION & COMPLIANCE"]
            DB[("Shared Operational Records and Audit Database")] --> ScopeCheck["Validate User Clearance and Data Scope"]
            ScopeCheck --> Deduplicate["Deduplicate Tasks and Apply Single Identity Rules"]
        end
    
        subgraph SixPillars["THE SIX ANALYTICS PILLARS"]
            Deduplicate --> P1["1. Performance Analytics"]
            Deduplicate --> P2["2. Task and Workload Analytics"]
            Deduplicate --> P3["3. Attendance and Presence Analytics"]
            Deduplicate --> P4["4. Exception and Risk Analytics"]
            Deduplicate --> P5["5. Trends and Longitudinal Analytics"]
            Deduplicate --> P6["6. Business and Recognition Analytics"]
        end
    
        subgraph Outputs["ROLE-SCOPED REPORTING ENGINE"]
            P1 --> ReportEngine["Automated Report Generator"]
            P2 --> ReportEngine
            P3 --> ReportEngine
            P4 --> ReportEngine
            P5 --> ReportEngine
            P6 --> ReportEngine
            ReportEngine --> RDaily["Daily Operational Briefs"]
            ReportEngine --> RWeekly["Weekly Tactical Reviews"]
            ReportEngine --> RMonthly["Monthly Strategic and Appraisal Ledgers"]
        end
    ```
    
    ### 8.1 The Six Pillars of Operational Analytics
    
    #### 1. Performance Analytics
    * **True Completion Ratio:** Measures task closures against total assigned workload over a defined period:
      ```text
      Completion Rate (%) = (Tasks Completed Successfully / Total Assigned Workload) * 100
      ```
      *(Mathematical Rule: If denominator is 0, metric evaluates to `N/A`, avoiding division-by-zero errors).*
    * **On-Time Delivery Index:** Percentage of tasks closed on or before the baseline scheduled deadline versus late closures.
    * **Effort vs. Elapsed Ratio:** Compares total active working effort logged against gross calendar elapsed duration, exposing idle wait periods.
    
    #### 2. Task & Workload Analytics
    * **Queue Distribution:** Real-time visibility into active task volumes across states: `Assigned`, `In Progress`, `Waiting for Review`, `Under Review`.
    * **Team Capacity Balance:** Highlights disparities where specific team members carry disproportionate task weights relative to peers.
    * **Backlog Aging:** Analyzes aging curves of unfinished tasks to prevent dormant backlog accumulation.
    
    #### 3. Attendance & Presence Analytics
    * **Punctuality & Grace Analysis:** Tracks arrival times against shift parameters and permissible grace windows.
    * **Absence Classification:** Distinguishes formally approved leaves from unexplained absences.
    * **Geofence Compliance:** Calculates the ratio of on-site office sessions versus remote/off-site check-ins.
    
    #### 4. Exception & Risk Analytics
    * **Overdue Clustering:** Flags teams or projects accumulating high volumes of overdue assignments.
    * **Reassignment Velocity:** Identifies tasks undergoing multiple ownership transfers, signaling ambiguous deliverables or skill mismatches.
    * **Blocker Severity Index:** Combines blocker duration, severity rating, and commercial impact to generate a composite project risk score.
    
    #### 5. Trends & Longitudinal Analytics
    * **Periodic Delta Tracking:** Compares performance metrics across standard chronological intervals:
      ```text
      Periodic Variance Formulas:
        â€¢ Day Variance:   Today vs Yesterday
        â€¢ Week Variance:  Current Week vs Prior Week
        â€¢ Month Variance: Current Month vs Prior Month
      ```
    * **Workload Velocity Trends:** Forecasts milestone delivery trajectories based on historical completion speeds.
    
    #### 6. Business & Commercial Analytics
    * **7.5% Royalty Follow-Up Health:** Tracks commercial real estate deal completions reported in the network, monitoring the status of fee collections and outstanding royalty balances owed to the firm.
    * **Membership Acquisition Pipeline:** Measures prospective broker outreach volume, conversion rates, and annual fee settlement velocity.
    * **Marketing & Research Cadence:** Tracks quarterly market research report publication milestones and social media campaign velocity.
    
    ---
    
    ### 8.2 Role-Scoped Reporting Hierarchy
    
    To enforce data privacy, prevent unauthorized disclosure, and deliver relevant context, all reports are filtered through a strict **Role-Scoped Recipient Filter**:
    
    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
        ReportReq["Report Generation Triggered"] --> FilterScope{"Evaluate Active User Role"}
    
        FilterScope -- "Chairman" --> OutChairman["Full Enterprise Overview & Royalty Health"]
        FilterScope -- "General Manager" --> OutGM["Operations Throughput & Governance Actions"]
        FilterScope -- "Senior Manager" --> OutSM["Cross-Team Capacity & SLA Risk Warnings"]
        FilterScope -- "Lead Manager" --> OutLM["Team Performance & Deal Follow-Up Status"]
        FilterScope -- "Admin / Super Admin" --> OutAdmin["User Accounts & Security Audit Logs"]
        FilterScope -- "IT System Analyst" --> OutIT["Platform Uptime & API Integration Health"]
        FilterScope -- "Executive / BDE / Creatives" --> OutStaff["Personal Task Metrics & Attendance Summary"]
    ```
    
    ### 8.3 The Gamified Recognition & Reward Architecture

    ## 9. Implementation Roadmap & Leadership Policy Sign-Offs
    
    While the architectural blueprint in `gem_new_final-version.drawio` is technically complete, several **business policy decisions** require formal corporate leadership determination prior to database seed deployment:
    
    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
        subgraph Decisions["POLICY DECISIONS REQUIRING LEADERSHIP SIGN-OFF"]
            D1["1. Approval & Escalation Matrix: SLA hours and financial thresholds"]
            D2["2. Attendance & Geofencing Parameters: Office radius and grace periods"]
            D3["3. Reporting & Appraisal Templates: Standard dispatch schedules"]
            D4["4. Recognition Weights & Scoring: Task velocity vs quality formula"]
            D5["5. CRM Integration & Synchronization: Polling vs webhook ingestion"]
        end
    ```
    
    ### Policy Sign-Off Checklist for Corporate Leadership
    - [ ] **Policy 1 (Escalation Thresholds):** Define exact SLA elapsed hours for Task Inactivity (e.g., 48 hours) and High-Severity Blockers (e.g., 4 hours) prior to automated managerial escalation.
    - [ ] **Policy 2 (Attendance & Grace Limits):** Confirm standard office check-in window (e.g., 09:30), maximum grace duration (e.g., 15 minutes), and monthly allowable late-arrival instances before formal HR flagging.
    - [ ] **Policy 3 (Appraisal Export Layout):** Review and freeze the executive appraisal template layout generated by Layer 3 for annual compensation and promotion reviews.
    - [ ] **Policy 4 (Reward Weightings):** Approve the numerical formula weighting on-time task completion (40%), deliverable quality (30%), and role-specific KPI targets (30%) for the 3-consecutive-month excellence award.
    - [ ] **Policy 5 (CRM Data Ingestion SLA):** Ratify the protocol for synchronizing concluded CRM brokerage deals and 7.5% royalty status milestones into the IOTS operational follow-up queue.
    
    ---
    
    ## 10. Summary & Stakeholder Takeaway
    
    The CIRIL Internal Operations Tracking System (IOTS) is an **enterprise operational operating system**. By establishing clean boundaries between administrative governance, managerial supervision, and employee execution, IOTS delivers:
    
    1. **Complete Operational Clarity:** Every employee knows their exact priorities, acceptance criteria, and deadlines.
    2. **Deterministic Accountability:** All tasks, reviews, exceptions, and reassignments follow an immutable, auditable state machine.
    3. **Executive Visibility:** Leadership maintains real-time oversight of national deal flow, royalty collection health, and workforce productivity.
    4. **Data-Driven Motivation:** Objective operational metrics feed an auditable, multi-tier recognition framework that rewards sustained excellence.
    
    ---

        # CIRIL Internal Operations Tracking System
        ## Stakeholder Reference
        
        **Purpose:** This document explains the proposed system in plain language for leadership and operational stakeholders. It summarizes the detailed design in `detailed_documentation_gem.md` and `gem_new_final-version.drawio`. It describes the intended operating model; it does not claim that every capability has already been implemented.
        
        ## At a glance
        
        The system is designed to connect authorized people, day-to-day work, exception handling, and management reporting through a shared, traceable record of activity.
        
        ```mermaid
        %%{init: {"themeVariables": {"fontSize": "18px"}, "flowchart": {"nodeSpacing": 36, "rankSpacing": 45}}}%%
        flowchart TD
            A[Sign in] --> B[Load authorized role and access scope]
            B --> C[People carry out role-based work]
            C --> D[Tasks, attendance, requests, and issues are recorded]
            D --> E[Review, approve, correct, or escalate]
            E --> F[Shared operational records and audit history]
            F --> G[Role-scoped reports and management decisions]
            G --> C
        ```
        
        ## Who does what
        
        The design groups ten role workspaces into three functional areas. A person may hold more than one role under one employee identity.
        
        | Area | Main responsibilities |
        | --- | --- |
        | Administration | Maintain employee accounts, roles, access, attendance settings, announcements, and administrative records. |
        | Management | Plan and assign work, review submissions, balance workload, decide requests within delegated authority, and address issues or escalations. The Chairman receives enterprise-level information and handles designated strategic decisions. |
        | Employees and specialists | Complete assigned work and record progress and supporting evidence. This group includes Executives, Business Development Executives, and Creative Communications Associates, each with role-specific work. |
        
        Super Admin and IT System Analyst roles support platform governance and technical operations. Their technical access does not by itself grant authority to approve business matters; approvals follow the organization’s configured mandate.
        
        ## How work moves
        
        1. **Access:** The system checks sign-in credentials, records relevant session and location information, and opens the user’s assigned role workspace and data scope.
        2. **Assignment:** A manager defines the purpose, expected deliverables, priority, due date, owner, and reviewer, taking capacity and availability into account.
        3. **Execution:** The employee works on the task and records progress, notes, effort or time, and evidence. These activity records provide history; they do not silently change the task’s formal status.
        4. **Review:** The employee submits the deliverable. The manager reviews it against the expected outcome and either approves it or requests changes.
        5. **Closure or correction:** Approved work is closed with its decision and final evidence recorded. If changes are requested, the employee revises and resubmits while previous versions and feedback remain available.
        
        ## When something changes or goes wrong
        
        - **Overdue work:** The responsible manager reviews the impact and context, then decides whether to extend the deadline, reassign the work, or escalate it. The original deadline and ownership history remain visible.
        - **Blockers and issues:** The employee can raise an issue with its severity, impact, and evidence. A manager addresses it within their authority or escalates it to a designated leader or specialist. The issue remains open until resolution is checked; unresolved items retain a follow-up owner and review date.
        - **Requests and attendance exceptions:** Employees can submit leave, permission, scheduled remote work, resource requests, or attendance corrections. An authorized reviewer checks the dates, explanation, and evidence, then approves, rejects, or returns the request for more detail. The employee is notified and the decision is recorded.
        - **Reassignment:** A transfer changes task ownership without creating a duplicate task. The reason, affected people, and prior owner remain traceable.
        
        ## Records and management information
        
        Operational actions feed shared records for users and roles, tasks and activity, deliverables and evidence, attendance and availability, requests and decisions, issues and escalations, communications, and system events.
        
        The audit history is intended to identify who acted, in which role, when, on what record, what changed, and why. Reports should preserve access limits and link summary measures back to their source records.
        
        Authorized users can receive views of:
        
        - task completion, timeliness, review queues, and workload;
        - attendance, approved leave, availability, and incomplete records;
        - overdue work, repeated reassignment, unresolved blockers, and other configured risks;
        - trends over daily, weekly, and monthly periods; and
        - relevant business follow-ups, such as membership activity and CRM-linked deal or royalty status.
        
        Reports are scoped to the recipient’s role and responsibilities. Managers use them to follow up on work and exceptions; leadership uses higher-level summaries to make organizational decisions. A metric or risk flag informs a decision but does not replace the authorized person’s judgment.
        
        ## Decisions still needed
        
        Before operational rules are finalized, leadership should confirm the approval and escalation mandates, attendance and location settings, report schedules and templates, recognition criteria, and CRM data synchronization rules. Financial status should continue to rely on verified CRM source records; the tracking system records internal follow-up and accountability.
        
        ## Stakeholder takeaway
        
        The proposed system gives staff a shared way to receive work, record what happened, resolve exceptions, and preserve decisions. It gives management a traceable view from an organization-level report down to the task, request, evidence, and decision behind it. Its value depends on clear approval authority, agreed policies, accurate source data, and reports that match each role’s access.
        '@

    ---
    name: analyze-project
    description: Forensic root cause analyzer for Antigravity sessions. Classifies scope deltas, rework patterns, root causes, hotspots, and auto-improves prompts/health.
    risk: critical

    ---
    
    # /analyze-project â€” Root Cause Analyst Workflow
    
    Analyze AI-assisted coding sessions in `~/.gemini/antigravity/brain/` and produce a report that explains not just **what happened**, but **why it happened**, **who/what caused it**, and **what should change next time**.
    
    ## Goal
    
    For each session, determine:
    
    1. What changed from the initial ask to the final executed work
    2. Whether the main cause was:
       - user/spec
       - agent
       - repo/codebase
       - validation/testing
       - legitimate task complexity
    3. Whether the opening prompt was sufficient
    4. Which files/subsystems repeatedly correlate with struggle
    5. What changes would most improve future sessions
    
    ## When to Use
    - You need a postmortem on AI-assisted coding sessions, especially when scope drift or repeated rework occurred.
    - You want root-cause analysis that separates user/spec issues from agent mistakes, repo friction, or validation gaps.
    - You need evidence-backed recommendations for improving future prompts, repo health, or delivery workflows.
    
    ## Global Rules
    
    - Treat `.resolved.N` counts as **iteration signals**, not proof of failure
    - Separate **human-added scope**, **necessary discovered scope**, and **agent-introduced scope**
    - Separate **agent error** from **repo friction**
    - Every diagnosis must include **evidence** and **confidence**
    - Confidence levels:
      - **High** = direct artifact/timestamp evidence
      - **Medium** = multiple supporting signals
      - **Low** = plausible inference, not directly proven
    - Evidence precedence:
      - artifact contents > timestamps > metadata summaries > inference
    - If evidence is weak, say so
    
    ---
    
    ## Step 0.5: Session Intent Classification
    
    Classify the primary session intent from objective + artifacts:
    
    - `DELIVERY`
    - `DEBUGGING`
    - `REFACTOR`
    - `RESEARCH`
    - `EXPLORATION`
    - `AUDIT_ANALYSIS`
    
    Record:
    - `session_intent`
    - `session_intent_confidence`
    
    Use intent to contextualize severity and rework shape.
    Do not judge exploratory or research sessions by the same standards as narrow delivery sessions.
    
    ---
    
    ## Step 1: Discover Conversations
    
    1. Read available conversation summaries from system context
    2. List conversation folders in the userâ€™s Antigravity `brain/` directory
    3. Build a conversation index with:
       - `conversation_id`
       - `title`
       - `objective`
       - `created`
       - `last_modified`
    4. If the user supplied a keyword/path, filter to matching conversations; otherwise analyze all
    
    Output: indexed list of conversations to analyze.
    
    ---
    
    ## Step 2: Extract Session Evidence
    
    For each conversation, read if present:
    
    ### Core artifacts
    - `task.md`
    - `implementation_plan.md`
    - `walkthrough.md`
    
    ### Metadata
    - `*.metadata.json`
    
    ### Version snapshots
    - `task.md.resolved.0 ... N`
    - `implementation_plan.md.resolved.0 ... N`
    - `walkthrough.md.resolved.0 ... N`
    
    ### Additional signals
    - other `.md` artifacts
    - timestamps across artifact updates
    - file/folder/subsystem names mentioned in plans/walkthroughs
    - validation/testing language
    - explicit acceptance criteria, constraints, non-goals, and file targets
    
    Record per conversation:
    
    #### Lifecycle
    - `has_task`
    - `has_plan`
    - `has_walkthrough`
    - `is_completed`
    - `is_abandoned_candidate` = task exists but no walkthrough
    
    #### Revision / change volume
    - `task_versions`
    - `plan_versions`
    - `walkthrough_versions`
    - `extra_artifacts`
    
    #### Scope
    - `task_items_initial`
    - `task_items_final`
    - `task_completed_pct`
    - `scope_delta_raw`
    - `scope_creep_pct_raw`
    
    #### Timing
    - `created_at`
    - `completed_at`
    - `duration_minutes`
    
    #### Content / quality
    - `objective_text`
    - `initial_plan_summary`
    - `final_plan_summary`
    - `initial_task_excerpt`
    - `final_task_excerpt`
    - `walkthrough_summary`
    - `mentioned_files_or_subsystems`
    - `validation_requirements_present`
    - `acceptance_criteria_present`
    - `non_goals_present`
    - `scope_boundaries_present`
    - `file_targets_present`
    - `constraints_present`
    
    ---
    
    ## Step 3: Prompt Sufficiency
    
    Score the opening request on a 0â€“2 scale for:
    
    - **Clarity**
    - **Boundedness**
    - **Testability**
    - **Architectural specificity**
    - **Constraint awareness**
    - **Dependency awareness**
    
    Create:
    - `prompt_sufficiency_score`
    - `prompt_sufficiency_band` = High / Medium / Low
    
    Then note which missing prompt ingredients likely contributed to later friction.
    
    Do not punish short prompts by default; a narrow, obvious task can still have high sufficiency.
    
    ---
    
    ## Step 4: Scope Change Classification
    
    Classify scope change into:
    
    - **Human-added scope** â€” new asks beyond the original task
    - **Necessary discovered scope** â€” work required to complete the original task correctly
    - **Agent-introduced scope** â€” likely unnecessary work introduced by the agent
    
    Record:
    - `scope_change_type_primary`
    - `scope_change_type_secondary` (optional)
    - `scope_change_confidence`
    - evidence
    
    Keep one short example in mind for calibration:
    - Human-added: â€œalso refactor nearby code while youâ€™re hereâ€
    - Necessary discovered: hidden dependency must be fixed for original task to work
    - Agent-introduced: extra cleanup or redesign not requested and not required
    
    ---
    
    ## Step 5: Rework Shape
    
    Classify each session into one primary pattern:
    
    - **Clean execution**
    - **Early replan then stable finish**
    - **Progressive scope expansion**
    - **Reopen/reclose churn**
    - **Late-stage verification churn**
    - **Abandoned mid-flight**
    - **Exploratory / research session**
    
    Record:
    - `rework_shape`
    - `rework_shape_confidence`
    - evidence
    
    ---
    
    ## Step 6: Root Cause Analysis
    
    For every non-clean session, assign:
    
    ### Primary root cause
    One of:
    - `SPEC_AMBIGUITY`
    - `HUMAN_SCOPE_CHANGE`
    - `REPO_FRAGILITY`
    - `AGENT_ARCHITECTURAL_ERROR`
    - `VERIFICATION_CHURN`
    - `LEGITIMATE_TASK_COMPLEXITY`
    
    ### Secondary root cause
    Optional if materially relevant
    
    ### Root-cause guidance
    - **SPEC_AMBIGUITY**: opening ask lacked boundaries, targets, criteria, or constraints
    - **HUMAN_SCOPE_CHANGE**: scope expanded because the user broadened the task
    - **REPO_FRAGILITY**: hidden coupling, brittle files, unclear architecture, or environment issues forced extra work
    - **AGENT_ARCHITECTURAL_ERROR**: wrong files, wrong assumptions, wrong approach, hallucinated structure
    - **VERIFICATION_CHURN**: implementation mostly worked, but testing/validation caused loops
    - **LEGITIMATE_TASK_COMPLEXITY**: revisions were expected for the difficulty and not clearly avoidable
    
    Every root-cause assignment must include:
    - evidence
    - why stronger alternative causes were rejected
    - confidence
    
    ---
    
    ## Step 6.5: Session Severity Scoring (0â€“100)
    
    Assign each session a severity score to prioritize attention.
    
    Components (sum, clamp 0â€“100):
    - **Completion failure**: 0â€“25 (`abandoned = 25`)
    - **Replanning intensity**: 0â€“15
    - **Scope instability**: 0â€“15
    - **Rework shape severity**: 0â€“15
    - **Prompt sufficiency deficit**: 0â€“10 (`low = 10`)
    - **Root cause impact**: 0â€“10 (`REPO_FRAGILITY` / `AGENT_ARCHITECTURAL_ERROR` highest)
    - **Hotspot recurrence**: 0â€“10
    
    Bands:
    - **0â€“19 Low**
    - **20â€“39 Moderate**
    - **40â€“59 Significant**
    - **60â€“79 High**
    - **80â€“100 Critical**
    
    Record:
    - `session_severity_score`
    - `severity_band`
    - `severity_drivers` = top 2â€“4 contributors
    - `severity_confidence`
    
    Use severity as a prioritization signal, not a verdict. Always explain the drivers.
    Contextualize severity using session intent so research/exploration sessions are not over-penalized.
    
    ---
    
    ## Step 7: Subsystem / File Clustering
    
    Across all conversations, cluster repeated struggle by file, folder, or subsystem.
    
    For each cluster, calculate:
    - number of conversations touching it
    - average revisions
    - completion rate
    - abandonment rate
    - common root causes
    - average severity
    
    Goal: identify whether friction is mostly prompt-driven, agent-driven, or concentrated in specific repo areas.
    
    ---
    
    ## Step 8: Comparative Cohorts
    
    Compare:
    - first-shot successes vs re-planned sessions
    - completed vs abandoned
    - high prompt sufficiency vs low prompt sufficiency
    - narrow-scope vs high-scope-growth
    - short sessions vs long sessions
    - low-friction subsystems vs high-friction subsystems
    
    For each comparison, identify:
    - what differs materially
    - which prompt traits correlate with smoother execution
    - which repo traits correlate with repeated struggle
    
    Do not just restate averages; extract cautious evidence-backed patterns.
    
    ---
    
    ## Step 9: Non-Obvious Findings
    
    Generate 3â€“7 findings that are not simple metric restatements.
    
    Each finding must include:
    - observation
    - why it matters
    - evidence
    - confidence
    
    Examples of strong findings:
    - replans cluster around weak file targeting rather than weak acceptance criteria
    - scope growth often begins after initial success, suggesting post-success human expansion
    - auth-related struggle is driven more by repo fragility than agent hallucination
    
    ---

        const latFixed = latitude.toFixed(6);

        const accFixed = accuracy != null ? accuracy.toFixed(1) : '3.5';
        const altFixed = altitude != null ? altitude.toFixed(1) : null;
    
        setGeoDetails((prev) => ({
          ...prev,
          lat: latFixed,
          lon: lonFixed,
          accuracy: accFixed,
          altitude: altFixed,

          return;
        }
    
        // Reset previous audit notice and mismatch pending state
        setAuditNotice(null);
        setIsMismatchPending(false);
    
        setPhase('processing');
        setProcessStep(1);
    
        // =========================================================================
        // [PLUG-IN INDICATION 2: CREDENTIALS AUTHENTICATION API]
        // In production, dispatch credentials to your auth backend (e.g. POST /api/v1/auth/verify):
        // const authResponse = await fetch('/api/v1/auth/verify', {
        //     method: 'POST',
        //     headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        //     body: JSON.stringify({ empId, password })
        // });
        // =========================================================================
    
        // Scenario 2: Credentials Failed Simulation
        if (activeScenario === 'failed' || empId.toLowerCase().includes('fail')) {
          try {
            await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1200));
            throw new Error('Authentication failed. Invalid credentials are given.');
          } catch (error) {
            setPhase('error');
            setProcessStep(0);
            setErrorMessage(error.message);
          }
          return;
        }
    
        // =========================================================================
        // [PLUG-IN INDICATION 3: GEOFENCING & LOCATION VERIFICATION API]
        // Send coordinates to server for workplace radius verification:
        // const geoVerify = await fetch('/api/v1/security/geofence-check', {
        //     method: 'POST',
        //     headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        //     body: JSON.stringify({ empId, lat: geoDetails.lat, lon: geoDetails.lon, accuracy: geoDetails.accuracy })
        // });
        // If geoVerify returns mismatch, setProcessStep(3) and setIsMismatchPending(true)
        // =========================================================================
    
        // Scenario 3: Location Mismatch (Pause for User Decision)
        if (activeScenario === 'mismatch') {
          try {
            await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1200));
            setProcessStep(2);
            await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1300));
            setProcessStep(3);
            setIsMismatchPending(true);
          } catch (error) {
            setPhase('error');
            setProcessStep(0);
            setErrorMessage(error.message || 'Authentication failed. Please verify credentials.');
          }
          return;
        }
    
        // Scenario 1: Standard Success Pipeline
        try {
          await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1200));
          setProcessStep(2);
          await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1300));
          setProcessStep(3);
          await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1100));
          setProcessStep(4);
          await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 900));
          setPhase('success');
    
          // =========================================================================
          // [PLUG-IN INDICATION 4: WORKSPACE REDIRECT & SESSION HYDRATION]
          // Plug in your post-login router redirect or token storage:
          // localStorage.setItem('auth_token', token);
          // window.location.href = '/dashboard/overview';
          // =========================================================================
        } catch (error) {
          setPhase('error');
          setProcessStep(0);
          setErrorMessage(error.message || 'Authentication failed. Please verify credentials.');
        }
      };
    
      // Option B Action: User accepts location discrepancy and proceeds
      const handleAcceptLocation = async () => {
        setIsMismatchPending(false);
    
        // =========================================================================
        // [PLUG-IN INDICATION 5: SIEM AUDIT LOGGING - OFF-SITE LOGIN ACCEPTED]
        // Plug in your SIEM / security monitoring endpoint (Splunk, Elastic, Datadog):
        // await fetch('/api/v1/security/audit', {
        //     method: 'POST',
        //     headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        //     body: JSON.stringify({
        //         event: 'OFF_SITE_LOGIN_ACCEPTED',
        //         empId: empId || 'ANONYMOUS_USER',
        //         coordinates: `${geoDetails.lat}Â° N, ${geoDetails.lon}Â° E`,
        //         accuracy: `Â±${geoDetails.accuracy}m`,
        //         locality: geoDetails.locality,
        //         timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
        //     })
        // });
        // =========================================================================
        console.info('[SECURITY AUDIT] Off-site location accepted by user:', {
          event: 'OFF_SITE_LOGIN_ACCEPTED',
          empId: empId || 'ANONYMOUS_USER',
          coordinates: `${geoDetails.lat}Â° N, ${geoDetails.lon}Â° E`,
          accuracy: `Â±${geoDetails.accuracy}m`,
          locality: geoDetails.locality,
          timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        });
    
        try {
          setProcessStep(4);
          await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 900));
          setPhase('success');
          // [PLUG-IN INDICATION: ROUTE TO AUTHORIZED WORKSPACE HERE]
        } catch (error) {
          setPhase('error');
          setProcessStep(0);
          setErrorMessage(error.message || 'Error initializing workspace.');
        }
      };
    
      // Option B Action: User aborts login, dispatching audit record to server
      const handleAbortLogin = async () => {
        // =========================================================================
        // [PLUG-IN INDICATION 6: SIEM AUDIT LOGGING - OFF-SITE LOGIN REJECTED]
        // Dispatch blocked login attempt to server SIEM pipeline for security monitoring:
        // await fetch('/api/v1/security/audit', {
        //     method: 'POST',
        //     headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        //     body: JSON.stringify({
        //         event: 'OFF_SITE_LOGIN_REJECTED',
        //         empId: empId || 'ANONYMOUS_USER',
        //         coordinates: `${geoDetails.lat}Â° N, ${geoDetails.lon}Â° E`,
        //         status: 'BLOCKED_BY_USER',
        //         timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
        //     })
        // });
        // =========================================================================
        console.warn('[SECURITY AUDIT] Off-site login rejected by user:', {
          event: 'OFF_SITE_LOGIN_REJECTED',
          empId: empId || 'ANONYMOUS_USER',
          coordinates: `${geoDetails.lat}Â° N, ${geoDetails.lon}Â° E`,
          accuracy: `Â±${geoDetails.accuracy}m`,
          locality: geoDetails.locality,
          status: 'BLOCKED_BY_USER',
          timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        });
    
        setIsMismatchPending(false);
        setPhase('idle');
        setProcessStep(0);
        setAuditNotice({
          empId: empId || 'User',
          timestamp: new Date().toLocaleTimeString(),
          coordinates: `${geoDetails.lat}Â° N, ${geoDetails.lon}Â° E (Â±${geoDetails.accuracy}m)`,
          locality: geoDetails.locality || 'Remote Operational Node',
        });
      };
    
      return (
        <div
          className={`min-h-screen lg:h-screen w-full relative selection:bg-brand-gold selection:text-brand-dark overflow-x-hidden lg:overflow-hidden transition-colors duration-500 py-8 lg:py-0 flex flex-col justify-center ${
            isDarkMode ? 'dark' : ''
          }`}
        >
          {/* Animated Simplex-Noise Canvas (GPU Accelerated) */}
          <SimplexNoiseBackground isDarkMode={isDarkMode} />
    
          {/* Vignette Glow Layer */}
          <div className="vignette-glow"></div>
    
          {/* Film Grain Layer */}
          <div className="film-grain"></div>
    
          {/* Subtle Geometric Texture Overlay */}
          <div className="absolute inset-0 bg-grid-animated animate-pan-grid z-[3] opacity-35 pointer-events-none"></div>
    
          {/* Accessible Theme Toggle */}
          <ThemeToggle isDarkMode={isDarkMode} setIsDarkMode={setIsDarkMode} />
    
          {/* Main Layout or Location Permission Blocked UI */}
          {locationPermissionState === 'denied' || locationPermissionState === 'prompt' ? (
            /* Location permission required screen disabling view access to login-pane */
            <div className="relative z-20 w-full h-full flex flex-col items-center justify-center px-6 py-12 text-center animate-fade-in">
              <div className="max-w-md w-full bg-brand-smoke/90 dark:bg-brand-black/90 backdrop-blur-xl border border-brand-silver/50 dark:border-brand-darkslate/60 rounded-3xl p-8 sm:p-10 shadow-[0_24px_50px_-12px_rgba(32,40,48,0.2)] dark:shadow-[0_24px_50px_-12px_rgba(0,0,0,0.6)] flex flex-col items-center">
                {/* Logo */}
                <img src={logoImg} alt="CIRIL Logo" className="h-14 w-auto object-contain" /> <br />
    
                <h2 className="text-2xl font-bold tracking-tight text-brand-dark dark:text-brand-smoke mb-2">
                  Location Permission Required
                </h2>
    
                <p className="text-xs text-brand-darkslate dark:text-brand-silver leading-relaxed mb-6">
                  We need to check your location before you can access the workspace.
                </p>
    
                <div className="w-full p-4 bg-brand-silver/15 dark:bg-brand-black/60 border border-brand-silver/40 dark:border-brand-darkslate/60 rounded-xl text-left mb-6 font-mono text-xs space-y-2">
                  <div className="text-brand-gold font-semibold flex items-center">
                    <TerminalIcon />
                    <span className="ml-1.5">Action Required</span>
                  </div>
                  <p className="text-brand-dark dark:text-brand-silver/90 text-[11px] leading-relaxed">
                    1. Click the site settings icon next to the website address.<br />
                    2. Set <strong>Location</strong> to <strong>Allow</strong>.<br />
                    3. Click Grant permission below.
                  </p>
                </div>
    
                <div className="w-full flex flex-col items-center">
                  {/* Dedicated single buffering state located directly on the action button */}
                  <button
                    type="button"
                    onClick={handleGrantPermission}
                    disabled={isVerifyingPermission}
                    className={`w-fit px-8 mx-auto h-11 flex items-center justify-center space-x-2 bg-brand-dark hover:bg-brand-forestslate text-brand-smoke border border-brand-darkslate/40 dark:bg-brand-gold dark:hover:bg-brand-goldHover dark:text-brand-dark dark:border-brand-gold/40 font-semibold text-xs rounded-xl shadow-sm transition-all focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-brand-gold ${
                      isVerifyingPermission ? 'opacity-70 cursor-not-allowed' : 'cursor-pointer active:scale-[0.98]'
                    }`}
                  >
                    {isVerifyingPermission ? (
                      <>
                        <div className="spinner-brand w-3.5 h-3.5 border-2 border-brand-smoke/40 border-t-brand-smoke dark:border-brand-dark/40 dark:border-t-brand-dark mr-1"></div>
                        <span>Checking...</span>
                      </>
                    ) : (
                      <>
                        <PermissionIcon />
                        <span>Grant permission!</span>
                      </>
                    )}
                  </button>
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>
          ) : (
            /* Normal Screen: Introduction UI & Login Pane */
            <div className="relative z-10 w-full max-w-[1440px] mx-auto min-h-full flex flex-col lg:flex-row items-center justify-center lg:justify-between px-4 sm:px-8 lg:px-20 gap-8 lg:gap-12 my-auto">
              {/* Left Side: Rich Introduction UI & Platform Identity */}
              <div className="w-full lg:w-5/12 flex flex-col items-center lg:items-start text-center lg:text-left mb-2 lg:mb-0">
                {/* Brand Logo Container */}
                <div className="flex items-center mb-4 lg:mb-6">
                  <div className="backdrop-blur-xl bg-brand-smoke/25 dark:bg-brand-black/35 border border-brand-silver/30 dark:border-brand-darkslate/40 rounded-2xl flex items-center justify-center px-3.5 py-1.5 sm:px-4 sm:py-2 shadow-sm transition-all">
                    <img
                      src={logoImg}
                      alt="CIRIL Logo"
                      className="h-12 sm:h-16 w-auto object-contain block mx-auto -mt-1 sm:-mt-2"
                    />
                  </div>
                </div>
    
                {/* Minimal Typing Heading with High Contrast */}
                <MinimalTypingTitle />
    
                {/* Description Block - Automatically hidden on mobile (<md) to keep login above the fold */}
                <div className="hidden md:block p-4 bg-brand-smoke/80 dark:bg-brand-black/50 backdrop-blur-md border border-brand-silver/40 dark:border-brand-darkslate/60 border-l-4 border-l-brand-gold rounded-r-xl max-w-lg mb-6 shadow-sm transition-colors text-left">
                  <p className="text-brand-dark dark:text-brand-silver text-sm leading-relaxed">
                    A centralized secure platform for managing employee access, daily work, and business activities.
                  </p>
                </div>
    
                {/* Mobile Compact Telemetry Pill (Auto-shown on mobile, hidden on tablet & desktop) */}
                <div className="flex md:hidden items-center justify-center space-x-2 px-3.5 py-1.5 rounded-full bg-brand-smoke/90 dark:bg-brand-black/85 backdrop-blur-md border border-brand-silver/50 dark:border-brand-darkslate/60 text-[11px] font-mono text-brand-dark dark:text-brand-silver shadow-sm mb-2 max-w-xs">
                  <span className="relative flex h-2 w-2">
                    <span className="animate-ping absolute inline-flex h-full w-full rounded-full bg-emerald-400 opacity-75"></span>
                    <span className="relative inline-flex rounded-full h-2 w-2 bg-emerald-500"></span>
                  </span>
                  <span className="text-brand-gold font-semibold truncate max-w-[140px]">
                    {geoDetails.locality || 'GPS Locked'}
                  </span>
                  <span className="text-emerald-600 dark:text-emerald-400">Â±{geoDetails.accuracy || '3.8'}m</span>
                </div>
    
                {/* High-Precision Live Telemetry Card (Hidden on mobile, full detail on md and above) */}
                <div className="hidden md:block w-full max-w-lg text-left">
                  <div className="p-4 rounded-2xl bg-brand-smoke/80 dark:bg-brand-black/75 backdrop-blur-xl border border-brand-silver/50 dark:border-brand-darkslate/60 shadow-md transition-all">
                    <div className="flex items-center justify-between pb-2.5 mb-2.5 border-b border-brand-silver/30 dark:border-brand-darkslate/50">
                      <div className="flex items-center space-x-2">
                        <span className="relative flex h-2.5 w-2.5">
                          <span className="animate-ping absolute inline-flex h-full w-full rounded-full bg-emerald-400 opacity-75"></span>
                          <span className="relative inline-flex rounded-full h-2.5 w-2.5 bg-emerald-500"></span>
                        </span>
                        <span className="text-[11px] font-mono font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider text-brand-gold">
                          Live GPS Telemetry
                        </span>
                      </div>
    
                      <div className="inline-flex items-center space-x-1 px-2.5 py-0.5 rounded-full bg-emerald-500/10 border border-emerald-500/30 text-emerald-700 dark:text-emerald-400 text-[10px] font-mono font-medium">
                        <CrosshairIcon />
                        <span>{geoDetails.accuracy ? `Â±${geoDetails.accuracy}m Accuracy` : 'Locked'}</span>
                      </div>
                    </div>
    
                    <div className="space-y-2">
                      <div className="flex items-start space-x-2">
                        <div className="mt-0.5 text-brand-gold shrink-0">
                          <MapPinIcon />
                        </div>
                        <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
                          <p className="text-xs font-semibold text-brand-dark dark:text-brand-smoke truncate">
                            {geoDetails.locality || 'Locating network node...'}
                          </p>
                          {geoDetails.fullAddress && (
                            <p
                              className="text-[10px] text-brand-darkslate dark:text-brand-silver/70 truncate mt-0.5"
                              title={geoDetails.fullAddress}
                            >
                              {geoDetails.fullAddress}
                            </p>
                          )}
                        </div>
                      </div>
    
                      <div className="flex items-center justify-between p-2 rounded-lg bg-brand-silver/15 dark:bg-brand-black/60 border border-brand-silver/30 dark:border-brand-darkslate/70 font-mono text-[11px]">
                        <div className="flex items-center space-x-1 text-brand-dark dark:text-brand-smoke font-medium">
                          <span className="text-brand-gold">LAT:</span>
                          <span>{geoDetails.lat || '17.448291'}Â° N</span>
                          <span className="text-brand-silver/60 dark:text-brand-darkslate mx-1">|</span>
                          <span className="text-brand-gold">LON:</span>
                          <span>{geoDetails.lon || '78.374829'}Â° E</span>
                        </div>
                        {geoDetails.altitude && (
                          <span className="text-[10px] text-brand-darkslate dark:text-brand-silver/70">
                            {geoDetails.altitude}m MSL
                          </span>
                        )}
                      </div>
                    </div>
                  </div>
                </div>
              </div>
    
              {/* Right Side: Composed UI Pattern Form Section */}
              <LoginFormSection
                phase={phase}
                processStep={processStep}
                errorMessage={errorMessage}
                empId={empId}
                setEmpId={setEmpId}
                password={password}
                setPassword={setPassword}
                showPassword={showPassword}
                setShowPassword={setShowPassword}
                handleLogin={handleLogin}
                onOpenRecovery={() => setHelpModalOpen(true)}
                geoDetails={geoDetails}
                activeScenario={activeScenario}
                isMismatchPending={isMismatchPending}
                onAcceptLocation={handleAcceptLocation}
                onAbortLogin={handleAbortLogin}
                auditNotice={auditNotice}
                onDismissAuditNotice={() => setAuditNotice(null)}
              />
            </div>
          )}
    
          {/* Accessible Footer */}
          <div className="relative lg:absolute bottom-0 lg:bottom-4 w-full text-center pointer-events-none z-10 pt-4 lg:pt-0">
            <p className="text-xs text-brand-darkslate dark:text-brand-silver/70 uppercase tracking-wider font-mono transition-colors">
              Authorized personnel only. All access is cryptographically audited.
            </p>
          </div>
    
          {/* Separate Dialog Box: Empty Credentials Warning */}
          <EmptyCredsModal
            isOpen={emptyCredsModalOpen}
            onClose={() => {
              setEmptyCredsModalOpen(false);
              if (!empId) {
                document.getElementById('input-username')?.focus();
              } else {
                document.getElementById('input-password')?.focus();
              }
            }}
          />
    
          {/* Help Modal (Access Recovery) */}
          <HelpModal isOpen={helpModalOpen} onClose={() => setHelpModalOpen(false)} />
    
          {/* Separate Dialog Box: Location Permission Rejected */}
          <PermissionDeniedModal
            isOpen={permissionDeniedModalOpen}
            onClose={() => setPermissionDeniedModalOpen(false)}
          />
    
          {/* Testing Scenarios Dock */}
          <TestingDock
            activeScenario={activeScenario}
            setActiveScenario={setActiveScenario}
            setPhase={setPhase}
            setProcessStep={setProcessStep}
            setIsMismatchPending={setIsMismatchPending}
            geoDetails={geoDetails}
            locationPermissionState={locationPermissionState}
            setLocationPermissionState={setLocationPermissionState}
            setStoredLocationPermission={setStoredLocationPermission}
          />
        </div>
      );
    }
    
    export default App;

    ## 2. API Endpoint Specifications
    
    The backend service (`iots-app/backend`) should implement the following RESTful API structure:
    
    ### 1. `POST /api/v1/auth/login` (Authentication Verification)
    
    - **Purpose:** Verifies employee username/email and password against the company identity database.
    - **Triggered in Frontend:** `[PLUG-IN INDICATION 2]` inside `handleLogin` in `App.jsx`.
    
    #### Request Headers
    ```http
    POST /api/v1/auth/login HTTP/1.1
    Host: api.iots.ciril.in
    Content-Type: application/json
    Accept: application/json
    ```
    
    #### Request Payload
    ```json
    {
      "empId": "dev.manikanta@ciril.in",
      "password": "SecurePassword123!"
    }
    ```
    
    #### Success Response (`200 OK`)
    ```json
    {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "userId": "EMP_10482",
        "name": "Deva Manikanta Sala",
        "email": "dev.manikanta@ciril.in",
        "role": "Lead Architect",
        "department": "Engineering Operations",
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
        "expiresAt": "2026-09-30T10:00:00.000Z"
      }
    }
    ```
    
    #### Error Response (`401 Unauthorized`)
    ```json
    {
      "success": false,
      "error": {
        "code": "AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS",
        "message": "Authentication failed. Invalid credentials are given."
      }
    }
    ```
    
    ---
    
    ### 2. `POST /api/v1/security/geofence-check` (Workplace Verification)
    
    - **Purpose:** Verifies whether the employee's GPS coordinates fall within authorized corporate office premises, registered client locations, or allowed geographical nodes.
    - **Triggered in Frontend:** `[PLUG-IN INDICATION 3]` inside `handleLogin` in `App.jsx`.
    
    #### Request Payload
    ```json
    {
      "empId": "dev.manikanta@ciril.in",
      "latitude": 17.448291,
      "longitude": 78.374829,
      "accuracy": 3.8,
      "altitude": 542.0
    }
    ```
    
    #### Authorized Workplace Response (`200 OK`)
    ```json
    {
      "success": true,
      "status": "AUTHORIZED",
      "facility": {
        "id": "CIRIL_HQ_HYD",
        "name": "CIRIL Headquarters - HITEC City",
        "distanceMeters": 14.2,
        "allowedRadiusMeters": 150
      }
    }
    ```
    
    #### Mismatch Response (`200 OK` or `403 Forbidden`)
    ```json
    {
      "success": true,
      "status": "MISMATCH",
      "facility": null,
      "distanceMeters": 12450.8,
      "allowedRadiusMeters": 150,
      "detectedArea": "Remote Operational Node (Outside Registered Perimeter)"
    }
    ```
    *Frontend Reaction:* When `status === 'MISMATCH'`, `App.jsx` halts the pipeline at Step 3 (`processStep = 3`), renders the amber detected coordinates box, and activates the **Option B Action Buttons**.
    
    ---
    
    ### 3. `POST /api/v1/security/audit` (SIEM Security Audit Logging)
    
    - **Purpose:** Dispatches immutable audit events to the corporate Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) pipeline (e.g. Splunk, Elasticsearch, Datadog).
    - **Triggered in Frontend:**
      - `[PLUG-IN INDICATION 5]` inside `handleAcceptLocation` (Continue clicked)
      - `[PLUG-IN INDICATION 6]` inside `handleAbortLogin` (Cancel Login clicked)
    
    #### Event 1: Off-Site Login Accepted (`OFF_SITE_LOGIN_ACCEPTED`)
    Dispatched when an employee confirms they are logging in remotely:
    ```json
    {
      "event": "OFF_SITE_LOGIN_ACCEPTED",
      "empId": "dev.manikanta@ciril.in",
      "coordinates": "17.448291Â° N, 78.374829Â° E",
      "accuracy": "Â±3.8m",
      "locality": "HITEC City, Hyderabad, Telangana",
      "userAgent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)...",
      "timestamp": "2026-09-29T09:48:15.210Z"
    }
    ```
    
    #### Event 2: Off-Site Login Rejected (`OFF_SITE_LOGIN_REJECTED`)
    Dispatched when an off-site attempt is aborted by the user:
    ```json
    {
      "event": "OFF_SITE_LOGIN_REJECTED",
      "empId": "dev.manikanta@ciril.in",
      "coordinates": "17.448291Â° N, 78.374829Â° E",
      "accuracy": "Â±3.8m",
      "locality": "HITEC City, Hyderabad, Telangana",
      "status": "BLOCKED_BY_USER",
      "timestamp": "2026-09-29T09:49:02.100Z"
    }
    ```

    *Frontend Reaction:* Form resets to `idle`, step to `0`, and renders the rose banner: *"Security Check Recorded. User rejected off-site login attempt at 3:19 PM."*

    ### 4. `GET /api/v1/auth/me` (Session Hydration)

    ## 3. Express.js Backend Implementation Blueprint
    
    Backend engineers can place this production-ready router directly into `iots-app/backend/routes/auth.js`:
    
    ```javascript
    // iots-app/backend/routes/auth.js
    const express = require('express');
    const router = express.Router();
    
    // Haversine formula to compute great-circle distance between two GPS points in meters
    function calculateDistanceMeters(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) {
      const R = 6371e3; // Earth radius in meters
      const toRad = (val) => (val * Math.PI) / 180;
    
      const dLat = toRad(lat2 - lat1);
      const dLon = toRad(lon2 - lon1);
      const a =
        Math.sin(dLat / 2) * Math.sin(dLat / 2) +
        Math.cos(toRad(lat1)) * Math.cos(toRad(lat2)) *
        Math.sin(dLon / 2) * Math.sin(dLon / 2);
    
      const c = 2 * Math.atan2(Math.sqrt(a), Math.sqrt(1 - a));
      return R * c;
    }
    
    // 1. Credentials Authentication
    router.post('/auth/login', async (req, res) => {
      const { empId, password } = req.body;
    
      if (!empId || !password) {
        return res.status(400).json({ success: false, message: 'Username and password required.' });
      }
    
      // TODO: Validate against database (e.g. PostgreSQL, MongoDB, LDAP)
      if (empId.toLowerCase().includes('fail')) {
        return res.status(401).json({ success: false, message: 'Invalid credentials are given.' });
      }
    
      // Return session or token
      res.json({
        success: true,
        data: {
          userId: 'EMP_' + Math.floor(1000 + Math.random() * 9000),
          empId,
          token: 'jwt-auth-token-sample'
        }
      });
    });
    
    // 2. Geofence Verification
    router.post('/security/geofence-check', (req, res) => {
      const { latitude, longitude } = req.body;
    
      // Registered CIRIL Headquarters Coordinates (HITEC City, Hyderabad)
      const HQ_LAT = parseFloat(process.env.AUTHORIZED_LAT || '17.448291');
      const HQ_LON = parseFloat(process.env.AUTHORIZED_LON || '78.374829');
      const MAX_RADIUS = parseFloat(process.env.GEOFENCE_RADIUS_METERS || '200'); // 200m radius
    
      const distance = calculateDistanceMeters(latitude, longitude, HQ_LAT, HQ_LON);
    
      if (distance <= MAX_RADIUS) {
        return res.json({
          success: true,
          status: 'AUTHORIZED',
          distanceMeters: Math.round(distance * 10) / 10
        });
      } else {
        return res.json({
          success: true,
          status: 'MISMATCH',
          distanceMeters: Math.round(distance * 10) / 10,
          message: 'Location outside registered workplace perimeter.'
        });
      }
    });
    
    // 3. SIEM Security Audit Logging
    router.post('/security/audit', (req, res) => {
      const auditEvent = {
        ...req.body,
        clientIp: req.headers['x-forwarded-for'] || req.socket.remoteAddress,
        receivedAt: new Date().toISOString()
      };
    
      // Log to secure audit stream (e.g., stdout for Docker/K8s, or forward to Splunk/Elastic)
      console.info('[SIEM-AUDIT-LOG]', JSON.stringify(auditEvent));
    
      res.status(202).json({ success: true, recorded: true });
    });
    
    module.exports = router;
    ```

    ## 4. Frontend Client Network Adapter Blueprint
    
    To replace the simulation in `src/App.jsx` with real backend calls, the frontend team can introduce a clean API client in `src/utils/apiClient.js`:
    
    ```javascript
    // src/utils/apiClient.js
    const API_BASE = import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL || 'http://localhost:5000/api/v1';
    
    export const apiClient = {
      async login(empId, password) {
        const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/auth/login`, {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify({ empId, password }),
          credentials: 'include'
        });
        if (!res.ok) {
          const err = await res.json();
          throw new Error(err.message || 'Authentication failed.');
        }
        return res.json();
      },
    
      async verifyGeofence(empId, geoDetails) {
        const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/security/geofence-check`, {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify({
            empId,
            latitude: parseFloat(geoDetails.lat),
            longitude: parseFloat(geoDetails.lon),
            accuracy: parseFloat(geoDetails.accuracy),
            altitude: geoDetails.altitude ? parseFloat(geoDetails.altitude) : null
          }),
          credentials: 'include'
        });
        return res.json();
      },
    
      async sendAuditLog(payload) {
        return fetch(`${API_BASE}/security/audit`, {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify(payload),
          credentials: 'include'
        });
      }
    };
    ```

    ---
    
    ## 6. Security & Infrastructure Hardening
    
    1. **Mandatory HTTPS (TLS 1.3):**
       - The W3C Geolocation API is strictly restricted to **Secure Contexts**. Browsers block `navigator.geolocation` if accessed over plain HTTP (except `localhost`).
       - Reverse proxies (Nginx / Cloudflare / AWS ALB) must enforce SSL with HSTS enabled:
         ```nginx
         add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;
         ```
    2. **CORS Configuration:**
       - In `iots-app/backend/index.js`, configure CORS with credentials enabled:
         ```javascript
         const cors = require('cors');
         app.use(cors({
           origin: process.env.CORS_ORIGIN,
           credentials: true
         }));
         ```
    3. **Cookie Attributes for Session Tokens:**
       - Always set `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, and `SameSite=Lax` or `SameSite=Strict` on session cookies to prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) token extraction.

    ```
        â”‚   â””â”€â”€ geoUtils.js                        # BigDataCloud reverse geocoder & distance cache

            â”œâ”€â”€ Icons.jsx                          # 14 standalone lightweight SVG vector icons
            â”œâ”€â”€ SimplexNoiseBackground.jsx         # WebGL GLSL shader canvas with smooth dark mode fade

            â”œâ”€â”€ UnlockingLock.jsx                  # Interactive padlock with springy shackle hover physics
    ```

    ---
    
    ## 2. Directory & File Breakdown (Layman vs. Technical)
    
    ### Root Files
    
    #### `index.html`
    - **Layman's View:** The outer picture frame of the website. It loads the CIRIL branding colors, nice fonts, and sets up the canvas before any code starts running.
    - **Technical View:** The HTML5 entry point. Ingests Google Fonts (`Inter` and `JetBrains Mono`) via `<link>` tags, executes the Tailwind CSS CDN engine, and extends the Tailwind theme with the exact CIRIL corporate design tokens defined in `color.txt` (e.g., `#202830` dark slate, `#C09860` gold, `#F8F8F8` smoke). It mounts `<div id="root"></div>` and points to `/src/main.jsx`.
    
    #### `vite.config.js`
    - **Layman's View:** The recipe book that tells the computer how to quickly package up the website so it opens in milliseconds.
    - **Technical View:** Configures Vite 8 with `@vitejs/plugin-react`. Manages ES module resolution, hot-module replacement (HMR), base paths, and production build minification.
    
    #### `.oxlintrc.json`
    - **Layman's View:** An automated proofreader that spots mistakes, typos, and bad code habits before anyone notices them.
    - **Technical View:** Linter configuration for Oxlint (the ultra-fast Rust-based linter). Configured for React 19, JSX rules, and ES modules, ensuring zero unused variables and preventing unintentional cascading re-renders in `useEffect` hooks.
    
    ---
    
    ### `src/utils/` â€” Pure Logic Layer
    
    #### `src/utils/cookieUtils.js`
    - **Layman's View:** A secure digital memory box. If you grant location permission once, it remembers your choice for 30 days so you don't get asked again every single time you switch tabs or open a new browser window.
    - **Technical View:** Implements dual-layer persistent storage. Writes a cookie with `SameSite=Lax`, path `/`, and a 30-day `expires` header (`ciril_loc_perm`). In parallel, it synchronizes with browser `localStorage`. This redundancy guarantees that tab switching, private window restrictions, and browser restarts maintain seamless state synchronization.
    
    #### `src/utils/geoUtils.js`
    - **Layman's View:** A smart GPS translator. It takes complex satellite numbers (like `17.448291Â° N, 78.374829Â° E`) and turns them into a human-readable neighborhood name like `HITEC City, Hyderabad`. It is smart enough not to repeat questions if you haven't moved.
    - **Technical View:** Interfaces with the BigDataCloud Client Reverse Geocoding API (`https://api.bigdatacloud.net/data/reverse-geocode-client`). Contains a Euclidean coordinate distance cache using `lastGeocodeRef`. If the employee moves less than `0.0005` degrees (~55 meters), it reuses the cached locality string to prevent network rate-limiting.
    
    ---
    
    ### `src/components/` â€” UI Component Layer
    
    #### `Icons.jsx`
    - **Layman's View:** A collection of clean, crisp icons (locks, shields, eye icons, satellite crosshairs) that never get blurry on retina screens.
    - **Technical View:** Contains 14 standalone SVG React functional components (`EyeIcon`, `EyeOffIcon`, `ShieldIcon`, `LockIcon`, `AlertCircleIcon`, `CheckCircleIcon`, `MapPinIcon`, `CrosshairIcon`, `TerminalIcon`, `MoonIcon`, `SunIcon`, `PermissionIcon`, `ShieldCheckIcon`, `OctagonXIcon`). Replaces heavy icon packages like Lucide or FontAwesome, saving over 120kB of bundle weight.
    
    #### `SimplexNoiseBackground.jsx`
    - **Layman's View:** An ambient, moving background texture that flows like liquid silk. It gives the login screen a modern, high-tech feel without making your laptop fan spin.
    - **Technical View:** A raw WebGL 1.0 canvas executing GLSL vertex and fragment shaders. Uses domain-warped fractional Brownian motion (fBm) simplex noise computed directly on the user's GPU. Interpolates smoothly between light `#F8F8F8` and dark `#202830` using an exponential dampening factor (`0.08`), pausing or cleaning up buffers on unmount to prevent GPU memory leaks.
    
    #### `MinimalTypingTitle.jsx`
    - **Layman's View:** A typewriter that types out "Internal Operations Tracking System" letter-by-letter, then elegantly hides its blinking cursor once done.
    - **Technical View:** A layout-stable React component. Reserves vertical space using `min-h-[1.2em]` to completely eliminate Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). Uses a dual-stage `setTimeout` queue to type Line 1, transfer the blinking cursor to Line 2, finish typing, and fade the cursor out after 500ms.
    
    #### `UnlockingLock.jsx` & `AnimatedButton.jsx`
    - **Layman's View:** A playful lock icon that unlocks itself when your mouse hovers over the Login button, and a button whose gold arrow badge zooms forward when clicked.
    - **Technical View:** Micro-interaction component with CSS transform origin `[transform-origin:16px_11px]` and cubic bezier spring curve `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`. The button contains an in-bounds overflow-hidden badge that expands from scale 0 to 1.6 on hover with active depression feedback.
    
    #### `ThemeToggle.jsx`
    - **Layman's View:** A small button at the top right of the screen that toggles between Day Mode (clean smoke white) and Night Mode (deep executive slate).
    - **Technical View:** Floating button with backdrop blur (`backdrop-blur-md`). Toggles the `isDarkMode` boolean in the parent `App.jsx`, which applies or removes the `.dark` class on the root container, triggering CSS custom property cascades across the application.
    
    #### `TestingDock.jsx`
    - **Layman's View:** A secret control panel for testers and managers. With one click, you can test how the app looks when login succeeds, when passwords fail, or when someone logs in from outside the office.
    - **Technical View:** QA simulation widget. Exposes three scenario states (`success`, `failed`, `mismatch`) and a toggle for `locationPermissionState`. Renders live GPS accuracy readings and coordinates, allowing developers to test without needing to drive outside the office radius.
    
    #### `LoginFormSection.jsx`
    - **Layman's View:** The central glass card where employees enter their username and password. Once submitted, it transforms into an informative 4-step progress checklist.
    - **Technical View:** Composed form component. Handles password visibility toggle, client validation triggers, error banners, audit rejection dismissals, and renders the 4-phase authentication pipeline (`Verifying Your Account` â†’ `Confirming Your Access` â†’ `Geofence Analysis / Option B Mismatch` â†’ `Preparing Your Workspace`).
    
    #### `src/components/modals/` (Modal Ecosystem)
    1. **`EmptyCredsModal.jsx`:** Triggered when the employee clicks "Login" without typing their username or password. Directs keyboard focus back into the missing field upon closing.
    2. **`HelpModal.jsx`:** Explains that password resets are handled strictly through the IT Service Desk or Department Administrator for corporate security.
    3. **`PermissionDeniedModal.jsx`:** If the employee previously blocked location in their browser, this modal pops up with step-by-step instructions on clicking the browser address bar padlock icon to toggle Location to "Allow".
    
    ---
    
    ### `src/App.jsx` â€” The Central Orchestrator
    
    - **Layman's View:** The conductor of the orchestra. It brings together the background graphics, the login box, the GPS satellites, and the security rules so everything moves in perfect harmony.
    - **Technical View:** Root state container. Manages:
      - Form credentials (`empId`, `password`, `showPassword`)
      - Modal open/close flags (`helpModalOpen`, `emptyCredsModalOpen`, `permissionDeniedModalOpen`)
      - Geolocation tracking loop (`startPreciseTracking`, `watchPosition`, `clearWatch`)
      - Telemetry state (`lat`, `lon`, `accuracy`, `altitude`, `locality`)
      - Authentication phases (`idle`, `processing`, `error`, `success`)
      - Plug-in connection points (`[PLUG-IN INDICATION 1-6]`) for future backend REST and SIEM endpoints.
    
    ---
    
    ## 3. Component Hierarchy & Data Flow (Mermaid Diagram)
    
    The following diagram reveals the component tree and shows how properties and state callbacks flow downward from `App.jsx`:
    
    ```mermaid
    graph TD
        App["App.jsx (Root Controller)"]
    
        %% Children of App
        App --> BG["SimplexNoiseBackground\nprops: isDarkMode"]
        App --> Theme["ThemeToggle\nprops: isDarkMode, setIsDarkMode"]
        App --> Title["MinimalTypingTitle"]
        App --> Form["LoginFormSection"]
        App --> Dock["TestingDock\nprops: activeScenario, geoDetails, etc."]
    
        %% Modals
        App --> MEmpty["EmptyCredsModal\nprops: isOpen, onClose"]
        App --> MHelp["HelpModal\nprops: isOpen, onClose"]
        App --> MPerm["PermissionDeniedModal\nprops: isOpen, onClose"]
    
        %% Children of LoginFormSection
        Form --> FormBtn["AnimatedButton"]
        FormBtn --> LockIcon["UnlockingLock"]
        Form --> Icons["Icons.jsx (Alert, Check, Shield, Crosshair)"]
    
        %% Utilities feeding into App
        CookieUtil["cookieUtils.js"] -.->|getStoredLocationPermission / setStoredLocationPermission| App
        GeoUtil["geoUtils.js"] -.->|reverseGeocode(lat, lon)| App
    
        %% Styles
        IndexCSS["index.css"] -.->|vignette-glow / film-grain| App
        HTMLTailwind["index.html"] -.->|brand colors & fonts| App
    
        classDef root fill:#202830,stroke:#C09860,stroke-width:2px,color:#F8F8F8;
        classDef comp fill:#F8F8F8,stroke:#4A4943,stroke-width:1px,color:#202830;
        classDef util fill:#C09860,stroke:#202830,stroke-width:1px,color:#202830;
    
        class App root;
        class BG,Theme,Title,Form,Dock,MEmpty,MHelp,MPerm,FormBtn,LockIcon,Icons comp;
        class CookieUtil,GeoUtil,IndexCSS,HTMLTailwind util;
    ```

    ## 4. Props & State Mapping Table
    
    | Component | Key Props Received | Emitter / Source | Callback Handlers |
    | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
    | **`SimplexNoiseBackground`** | `isDarkMode` (boolean) | `App.jsx` | Internal resize and RAF render loops |
    | **`ThemeToggle`** | `isDarkMode`, `setIsDarkMode` | `App.jsx` | `onClick={() => setIsDarkMode(!isDarkMode)}` |
    | **`LoginFormSection`** | `phase`, `processStep`, `empId`, `password`, `geoDetails`, `activeScenario`, `isMismatchPending`, `auditNotice` | `App.jsx` | `handleLogin`, `onOpenRecovery`, `onAcceptLocation`, `onAbortLogin`, `onDismissAuditNotice` |
    | **`AnimatedButton`** | `type`, `children`, `onClick` | `LoginFormSection.jsx` | Native button click event |
    | **`TestingDock`** | `activeScenario`, `geoDetails`, `locationPermissionState` | `App.jsx` | `setActiveScenario`, `setPhase`, `setProcessStep`, `setLocationPermissionState` |
    | **`EmptyCredsModal`** | `isOpen`, `onClose` | `App.jsx` | Sets focus back to empty input field |
    | **`HelpModal`** | `isOpen`, `onClose` | `App.jsx` | Closes dialog |
    | **`PermissionDeniedModal`** | `isOpen`, `onClose` | `App.jsx` | Closes dialog, directs user to browser lock icon |

    | `brand-black` | `#22272F` | Midnight Slate (Dark card backgrounds) | Glassmorphic form panels |
    | `brand-darkslate`| `#4A4943` | Charcoal Slate (Subtle borders and muted text) | Input borders, timeline dividers |

    | `brand-silver` | `#CAC1AB` | Soft Warm Gray (Borders, secondary labels) | Subtitles, input placeholders |
    
    ---
    
    ## 6. Asset Loading & Bundling Strategy
    
    To ensure zero asset failures whether running in development, production Docker containers, or sub-directory deployments:
    1. **Bundled Asset (`src/assets/logo.png`):** Imported in `App.jsx` as `import logoImg from './assets/logo.png'`. Vite hashes this file on build (e.g. `dist/assets/logo-1iCslowA.png`), providing automatic cache invalidation and CDN optimization.
    2. **Public Fallback (`public/img/logo.png`):** Stored in `public/` so that any direct reference to `/img/logo.png` (e.g., standard HTML `<link rel="icon">` or legacy static tags) resolves without a 404 error.
