    {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Warning: fs was declared with const; use let for reassignable variables.\nWarning: base was declared with const; use let for reassignable variables.\n\n===== IOTS_Tracking_Metrics_and_Evidence_Specification_Claude_version.docx =====\nCIRIL INTERNAL OPERATIONS TRACKING SYSTEM (IOTS)\nPerformance Tracking, Metrics and Evidence Specification\nWhat every role is measured on, how each number is calculated, and what proof backs it up. Written to design the role dashboards.\nItem\nDetail\nDate\nOctober 13, 2026\nStatus\nWorking draft for dashboard design. Targets and thresholds are proposals until the decisions in section 10 are made.\nBuilt from\niots-system.drawio, IOTS_DRAWIO_SYSTEM_STEP_BY_STEP_PLAN.md, FRONTEND_BACKEND_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md, and the earlier tracking_draft_gemini.docx\nSuggested location\ndocumentation\\plan\\\nRoles covered\nChairman, General Manager, Senior Manager, Lead Manager, Executive, BDE, Creatives Communication Associate, Admin, Super Admin, IT System Analyst\n\n1. What this document is for\nThis is the working spec for how IOTS tracks people and work. It tells you, for every role, what gets measured, how each number is calculated, where the raw data comes from, and what proof backs it up. The point is that you can open it while designing a dashboard and know exactly which widgets to build and which records feed them.\nIt rebuilds the earlier Gemini draft against the system diagram (iots-system.drawio) and the integration plan. Where the draft contradicted the diagram, the diagram won. The list of corrections is in Appendix A.\nHow to read the numbers in this document\nStated in the diagram: the three layers, the ten role workspaces, the task lifecycle, the metric rules (N/A on zero denominator, \"Target not configured\"), the audit contract, and the report types.\nProposed here: every target, threshold, time limit and weight. They are starting values that live in configuration, not business rules. The diagram says approval mandates, shifts, grace periods, report timing and recognition scoring stay configurable, so nothing in the code should hard-code them.\nNot set: where no sensible starting value exists, the target column says so. The system then shows \"Target not configured\", which is the intended behavior.\n\nRole count. The diagram defines ten role workspaces: Admin, Super Admin, IT System Analyst, Chairman, General Manager, Senior Manager, Lead Manager, Executive, BDE, and Creatives Communication Associate. The frontend has eleven dashboard components because social media and design are separate screens. This spec treats them as two views of one Creatives role (section 4.7).\n2. How tracking actually works\nEvery number on every dashboard comes from the same five-step chain. If a metric cannot be traced through all five steps, it should not be on a dashboard.\nStep\nWhat happens\nRule that keeps it honest\n1. Capture\nA person or the system does something: logs in, checks in, adds a note, submits work, approves a request, imports a CRM deal.\nEvery action carries employee ID and active role. People only enter facts; they never type a metric.\n2. Record\nThe API writes an append-only record (task activity, attendance event, evidence record, decision, audit event).\nRecords are never edited in place. Corrections are new records linked to the original, with who, why and when.\n3. Compute\nThe metric engine reads records for a chosen period and scope and applies the configured rules.\nTasks are counted once. Zero denominator gives N/A. Missing target gives \"Target not configured\". Rule and target versions are kept.\n4. Present\nDashboards and reports show the value together with its numerator, denominator, period and scope.\nOutput is limited to the viewer's role scope. Exports and report generation are logged.\n5. Act\nAn authorised person reviews a flag, opens the evidence, decides, and the decision is recorded.\nRules flag risk; people decide. The decision becomes a new record and feeds the next report.\n\n2.1 Events that feed the metrics\nEvent\nWho creates it\nRecord written\nMetrics it feeds\nLogin and location check\nAuth service\nSession record plus audit event with ONSITE / REMOTE / unknown tag\nLocation trends, auth anomalies, attendance context\nCheck-in / check-out\nEmployee\nAttendance event (kept separate from session and from task effort)\nAttendance rate, punctuality, working hours\nAvailability change\nEmployee\nAvailability log entry with start and end time\nLive roster, availability patterns\nTask created and assigned\nManager\nTask with deliverables, priority, due date, original due date, estimate, reviewer, evidence checklist\nAssignment velocity, load, utilisation\nProgress, note, effort, file\nAssignee\nTask activity record. Never changes task state.\nUpdate compliance, effort, last-activity age\nSubmission\nAssignee\nState change to Waiting for Review plus a numbered submission version\nOn-time delivery, submission count\nReview decision\nReviewer\nState change (Closed or Revision Required) with decision and reason\nReview latency, revision rate, first-time acceptance\nDeadline extension\nManager\nExtension record; original due date stays on the task\nExtension rate, on-time against both dates\nReassignment\nManager\nReassignment record: prior owner, new owner, reason, capacity check\nTransfer counts, owner history, load balance\nBlocker / issue\nAssignee or manager\nIssue linked to a task with severity, business impact and evidence\nBlocker age, escalation resolution time\nRequest\nEmployee\nRequest (leave, permission, scheduled remote, resource, correction) plus decision history\nRequest response time, approved absence\nConfig change\nAdmin / Super Admin\nAudit event with before and after values\nGovernance metrics, rule version history\nCRM import\nIntegration\nDeal reference with CRM source ID and verification time\nDeal flow, royalty due and collected\nHealth probe / deployment\nPlatform\nHealth record, incident, deployment or migration record\nUptime, latency, incident resolution time\n\n2.2 Standard metric definitions\nEvery role section below reuses these definitions. Define them once in the metric engine so a \"completion rate\" means the same thing on the Chairman's screen and an Executive's screen.\nMetric\nFormula\nCounting rules\nTask completion rate\nTasks approved and closed ÷ tasks assigned to the person that fell due in the period\nA reassigned task counts once, for the owner at the time it closes. Cancelled tasks are excluded and listed separately.\nOn-time delivery rate\nClosed tasks whose first submission was at or before the current approved due date ÷ closed tasks\nMeasured at submission, not at approval, so a slow reviewer never makes an employee late. Also show the rate against the original due date so extensions cannot hide lateness.\nRevision rate\nReview decisions that requested changes ÷ review decisions\nCounts decisions, so a task revised twice counts twice. Shows the average revisions per task next to it.\nFirst-time acceptance\nTasks closed with no changes requested ÷ tasks closed\nThe task-level counterpart of the revision rate.\nOverdue rate\nOpen tasks past current due date ÷ all open tasks\nAgeing buckets: 0 to 1 day, 2 to 3, 4 to 7, over 7. Waiting-for-review time is shown separately so overdue caused by a review queue is visible as such.\nElapsed vs active effort\nElapsed = closed time − assigned time. Effort = sum of logged effort minutes.\nReported as two figures, never one blended number. A big gap points to waiting, blockers or missing time logs.\nUpdate compliance\nWorking days with at least one activity record ÷ working days with at least one active task\nApproved leave days are removed from both sides.\nPlanned utilisation\nEstimated hours on open tasks due in the period ÷ available hours\nAvailable hours = shift hours minus approved leave and recorded breaks. Needs an estimate on every task.\nAttendance rate\nWorking days with a complete check-in and check-out ÷ scheduled working days\nApproved leave is removed from the denominator and shown separately from unexplained absence. Incomplete records are flagged, not counted as present.\nPunctuality\nCheck-ins within the configured grace window ÷ days present\nShift and grace rules come from Admin configuration.\nReview latency\nReview decision time − submission time, in business hours\nReported as median and 90th percentile. Applies to anyone who reviews.\nRequest response time\nDecision time − request time, in business hours\n\"Returned for detail\" stops the clock until the employee resubmits.\nBlocker resolution time\nResolution confirmed − issue raised\nExternal blockers keep their context label so they are not charged to the employee.\nEvidence completeness\nClosed tasks whose required evidence was accepted ÷ closed tasks that required evidence\nA task cannot close with a rejected or missing required item, so this should sit near 100%. A drop means a gate has a hole.\n\n2.3 Rules every dashboard follows\nShow the working. Each metric displays its value, numerator, denominator, period and scope. Click-through goes team, then employee, then task / request / attendance, then activity, then evidence, then decision and audit history.\nZero denominator shows \"N/A\", and a missing target shows \"Target not configured\". Never show 0%, NaN or an empty cell.\nSmall samples show counts. If the denominator is below a configured minimum (starting value 5), display \"3 of 4\" rather than \"75%\".\nContext stays attached. Approved leave and external blockers are labelled, not silently removed. Extensions keep the original deadline. Reassignment keeps the prior owner's overdue history on the task.\nTargets, deadlines and rules are versioned. A closed period keeps the rule version it was computed under. Changing a target next month does not rewrite last month.\nSelf-reported progress is a soft signal. A \"70% done\" slider is useful context but is not used for scoring or risk rules. Rules rely on timestamps, states and evidence.\nFlags explain themselves. Every risk flag lists the rule that fired and links to the records behind it.\n2.4 Who sees what\nThe diagram says roles are separate workspaces, not a reporting ladder, and that approval authority follows configured mandates, not job titles. The table is the default scope for dashboard design; the actual scope is read from the user's permissions on the server.\nRole\nDefault data scope\nEmployee-level detail\nNotes\nChairman\nWhole organisation\nOpens from Requires Attention, recognition and appraisal exports\nSummary first. Does not reassign tasks or reset accounts.\nGeneral Manager\nOrganisation operations, all member offices\nYes, all employees\nThe detailed monitoring view (section 5).\nSenior Manager\nTeams under the cross-team mandate\nYes, those teams\nComparison and capacity across operations, BD and creatives.\nLead Manager\nOwn teams\nYes, own team members\nDay-to-day assignment, review and follow-up.\nExecutive / BDE / Creatives\nOwn records only\nSelf\nPersonal services: attendance, requests, performance, security.\nAdmin\nAccounts, attendance, location, organisational oversight\nAccount and attendance level; global task oversight\nDoes not approve business deliverables or leave on privilege alone.\nSuper Admin and IT Analyst\nPlatform governance, full audit\nAudit level\nEqual platform privileges. Business approvals need a separate mandate.\n\n3. The evidence system\nEvidence is what lets a manager, an auditor or the Chairman reach the source behind any number. The rule is simple: a task cannot move forward on someone's word alone. The system enforces it at two gates, not by trusting reviewers to remember.\nGate\nWhat the system checks\nSubmission gate\nThe task cannot move to Waiting for Review until every required evidence slot on its checklist has a submitted item. The checklist is chosen by the manager when the task is created, from a template for the task type.\nClosure gate\nThe task cannot move to Closed until the reviewer has accepted every required item and recorded the decision. The reviewer cannot be the person who submitted the work.\n\n3.1 Evidence types\nThe draft used four \"tiers\". Types describe the evidence better than a ranking does, because a signed agreement is not \"higher\" than a call log; they are just different kinds of proof.\nType\nWhat it is\nTypical content\nWho accepts it\nWork artifact\nA file or link that is the deliverable\nDocument, deck, spreadsheet, design file, report, design link. Each upload is a numbered version with a file hash.\nThe task reviewer\nLocation proof\nProof of presence at a place\nCoordinates and accuracy at check-in, or a site-visit photo with its timestamp. Only collected where the task type or attendance rule requires it.\nAutomatic check against the configured location, then the reviewer for field visits\nExternal confirmation\nA record from outside IOTS\nCRM lead or deal ID, signed agreement, bank payment advice, statutory filing receipt. IOTS stores the reference and the time it was verified; CRM stays the financial source of truth.\nThe role named in the policy (for example GM for agreements, accounts for payments)\nOutreach log\nA dated record of contact\nCall outcome, email thread, WhatsApp campaign proof, meeting note, next follow-up date.\nLead Manager sampling, plus automatic checks for dated follow-ups\nPublication proof\nProof that something went live or was distributed\nLive link, screenshot, print or distribution record, final version link.\nThe reviewer who approved the asset\nSystem record\nGenerated by the platform itself\nAudit event, timer, health probe, deployment or migration record, incident log.\nAccepted automatically; reviewed by IT Analyst or Super Admin when disputed\nDecision record\nThe evidence that a human decided\nApproval, rejection, return-for-detail, with reason, reviewer, time and active role.\nIt is the decision; it cannot be edited, only followed by another record\n\n3.2 What every evidence record stores\nField\nPurpose\nevidenceId, type\nUnique ID and one of the seven types above\nlinkedEntity (kind + ID)\nThe task, request, deal, issue, attendance record or announcement it proves. Every item links to exactly one parent so nothing floats unattached.\nsubmittedBy, activeRole, submittedAt\nWho, in which role, when. Matches the audit contract (identity + active role + time).\nversion\nIncrements on each replacement. Earlier versions are kept and stay viewable.\nstorageRef, fileHash\nWhere the file lives and its hash, so a later swap is detectable. Links to CRM or external systems store the source ID and verification time instead.\nstatus\nSubmitted, Accepted, Rejected or Superseded\nreviewedBy, reviewedAt, reason\nRequired on Accepted and Rejected. A rejection must state what to fix.\n\nRejected and superseded items are never deleted. A reviewer reading a third submission can see the first two and the feedback given on each.\n3.3 Evidence by role\nRole\nProduces\nReviews or accepts\nDashboard shows\nExecutive\nWork artifacts, progress notes, effort entries, blocker evidence, field proof when the task type needs it\nNothing\nOwn items by status, rejected items needing a fix\nBDE\nOutreach logs, verified-contact sources, follow-up dates, meeting notes, CRM lead references\nNothing\nOwn outreach log and overdue follow-ups\nCreatives\nVersioned design and content files, proofreading notes, publication links, distribution records\nNothing\nVersion history per asset, publication proof status\nLead Manager\nReview decisions, written corrections, evaluation notes, request decisions, royalty follow-up records\nTeam deliverables, outreach samples, attendance and leave evidence\nReview queue by age, evidence waiting for a decision\nSenior Manager\nReassignment and capacity decisions with reasons, escalation decisions\nHigh-impact escalations from Lead Managers\nDecisions pending and decisions with no recorded reason\nGeneral Manager\nMinutes, resolutions, filing receipts, signed agreements, escalation notes\nExternal confirmations for agreements; escalations across teams\nGovernance items by status and the proof attached\nChairman\nRecognition sign-off, appraisal exports, enterprise announcements\nThree-month recognition evidence\nSign-off queue with the evidence pack behind each name\nAdmin\nOnboarding records, geofence configuration records, attendance corrections with reasons, announcement records\nAttendance exceptions and corrections\nExceptions awaiting resolution, with original and corrected record side by side\nSuper Admin\nAccess governance certificate, config change approvals with rationale\nHigh-level account changes, export policy\nConfig changes and exports with their reasons\nIT Analyst\nProbes, incident logs, post-incident write-ups, deployment and migration records\nTechnical incident resolutions\nIncidents with root cause and recovery verification\n\n4. Role-by-role tracking specification\nRoles run top-down so the monitoring layers come first, followed by the people whose work they monitor. Starting targets are proposals and every one is configurable. \"Not set\" means management needs to decide.\n4.1 Chairman\nPurpose: a ten-second read of organisational health, plus a way to open any number down to its source. Not a place for routine resets or task reassignment.\nWhat the dashboard needs to show\nEnterprise health strip: on-time delivery, completion, overdue share, each with trend against the prior period.\nRequires Attention panel: overdue clusters, repeated transfers, unresolved blockers. Each item says why it is flagged and links to evidence.\nRoyalty health: due, collected and outstanding by zone and month.\nAttendance summary: present, late, and remote / unknown-location share, with the count of unreviewed exceptions.\nRecognition queue: employees who have hit three qualifying months, with the evidence pack, awaiting sign-off.\nReports and appraisal-format exports, and enterprise announcements.\nData completeness note: how many tiles are currently N/A or \"Target not configured\", so a blank tile is never mistaken for good news.\nMetrics\nMetric\nFormula and denominator\nMeasured from\nEvidence / drill-down\nStarting target (proposed)\nEnterprise on-time delivery\nClosed tasks first-submitted by current due date ÷ closed tasks, all teams\nTask submission and due-date records\nTeam breakdown, then task list\n≥ 90%\nEnterprise completion rate\nStandard definition across all teams\nTask states\nTeam, then employee, then task\n≥ 90%\nOverdue inventory\nOpen overdue tasks, count and share, split by age and priority\nOpen tasks vs due dates\nOverdue list with owner, reviewer and last activity\nNot set\nOverdue clusters\nTeams or managers with N or more overdue tasks in the same window\nOverdue flags grouped by team\nThe tasks in the cluster\nN not set\nRepeated transfers\nTasks reassigned two or more times\nReassignment records\nOwner history and reasons\nNot set\nUnresolved blockers\nOpen issues by severity and age\nIssue records\nIssue, evidence, owner, next review date\nNone above High older than 2 days\nRoyalty due / collected / outstanding\nDue = 7.5% of each party's brokerage share. Collected = verified payments. Outstanding = due − collected.\nCRM-imported deals plus payment confirmations\nDeal, CRM source ID, payment evidence\nCollected by the agreed date\nAttendance health\nAttendance rate, punctuality, remote / unknown share, unreviewed exceptions\nAttendance events and flags\nTeam, then employee, then daily record\nNot set\nRecognition pipeline\nEmployees with 3 consecutive qualifying months awaiting sign-off\nMonthly recognition results\nEvidence pack per employee\nEvery case decided within one cycle\n\nAlerts this role receives\nCritical items (section 6) reach the Chairman immediately; everything else is in the digest.\n4.2 General Manager\nPurpose: the detailed operating view. The Chairman sees the weather; the GM sees who is doing what today. The IOTS platform handles this elegantly:\nUnified Authentication: The user logs in once with their master corporate credentials.\nAccount Profile Evaluation: The system detects all authorised system roles.\nDefault Landing: The user lands on their primary role dashboard.\nInstant Context Switcher: A prominent dropdown in the global navigation bar allows the user to switch between authorised workspaces in a single click.\nSession & Audit Segregation: Every audit log entry captures both the employee’s identity and the active role context under which the action was performed.\n\n\n===== tracking_draft_gemini.docx =====\nCIRIL INTERNAL OPERATIONS TRACKING SYSTEM (IOTS)\nMaster Engineering Specification: Operational Tracking, Performance Metrics & Multi-Role Evidence Architecture\nSystem Version: 2.0 Enterprise Release | Target System: iots-app (Vite 8 React + Express 5 Node.js API Gateway)\nDocument Classification\nArchitectural Scope\nTarget Roles Covered\nPrimary Reference\nInternal Engineering Spec\nLayers 1, 2, and 3 Telemetry\nAll 11 Organizational Roles\niots-system.drawio\n\n1. Executive Overview & The 3-Layer Tracking Architecture\nOperational tracking within the Commercial Real Estate Institutional Alliance (CIRIL) is built on an uncompromising principle: Complete Transparency, Absolute Accountability, and Cryptographic Evidence. Large commercial property transactions, inter-city tenant handshakes, and brokerage collections require every team member to operate with military precision.\nArchitectural Core Philosophy: Layman Flight Control Center Analogy\nThink of an international airport flight operations center. The Airport Chairman needs a 30-second macro radar showing all flight sectors, delays, and runway safety without baggage-handling details. The General Manager needs detailed operational surveillance over fuel, maintenance, air traffic control, and terminal throughput. Meanwhile, the pilots, ground crew, and mechanics require precision workbenches where every turn of a wrench, inspection report, and pre-flight checklist is logged with immutable proof. IOTS implements this exact paradigm.\nThe entire tracking system operates across three synchronized layers defined in iots-system.drawio:\nLayer 1 (Security, Geofencing & Authentication): Hardware GPS perimeter checks, IP address logging, and cryptographically verified employee credentials without public registration. Transparently tags sessions as ONSITE (within 350m of Hyderabad HQ) or REMOTE without disrupting legitimate off-site work.\nLayer 2 (Management, Operations & Execution): Daily work allocation, task lifecycle state transitions, time tracking, live team availability rosters, and the multi-role Evidence Collection Engine. Enforces the golden rule: Work Activity ≠ Task State.\nLayer 3 (Intelligence, Analytics & Reporting): Role-scoped analytics digests, SLA calculation engines, exception/risk radars, commercial 7.5% royalty calculations, and objective employee recognition algorithms (Star Performer of the Month).\n\n2. Core Engineering Invariants & Metric Engine Rules\nTo prevent metric corruption, gaming, and artificial workload inflation, the tracking engine enforces five non-negotiable architectural invariants:\nArchitectural Invariant\nSystem-Level Rule\nEngineering Enforcement & Fail-Safe\nInvariant 1: Work Activity ≠ Task State\nAdding notes, effort hours, or uploading attachments are historical activity entries. They NEVER mutate the task status directly.\nTask states (ASSIGNED → IN_PROGRESS → WAITING_FOR_REVIEW → UNDER_REVIEW → CLOSED) can only transition via explicit lifecycle state machine mutations authorized by the assigned actor or manager.\nInvariant 2: Stable Task Identity\nReassigning or transferring a task never creates a duplicate task entity or resets historical duration.\nThe task maintains its unique taskId throughout its entire lifecycle. A ReassignmentRecord is appended preserving original dueDate, prior assignee, and delay history.\nInvariant 3: Zero Denominator Handling\nNo metric calculation may divide by zero or emit NaN / null values into executive dashboards.\nIf total tasks or denominator is zero, the calculation engine outputs 'N/A' (Not Applicable). If no target is set, outputs 'Target Not Configured' rather than 0%.\nInvariant 4: CRM Financial Boundary\nThe external CRM remains the sole authoritative source of truth for commercial deal closing and broker fee totals.\nIOTS imports verified CRM records and strictly tracks internal operational task execution, lead giver (30%) / receiver (70%) follow-ups, and computes CIRIL's 7.5% royalty.\nInvariant 5: Authority Boundary\nAdministrative privilege alone does not approve business deliverables, leave requests, or commercial terms.\nSuper Admin and IT Analyst control platform infrastructure; business approvals strictly follow configured managerial reporting hierarchies (Lead Manager → Senior Manager → GM).\n\n3. The Universal Evidence System Architecture\nA fundamental requirement of IOTS is that no task can be marked 'Completed' or 'Closed' based on subjective word of mouth. Every operational action requires verifiable evidence. The Evidence System provides four distinct tiers of proof:\nEvidence Tier\nEvidence Classification\nRequired Artifact / Payload\nVerification & QA Gate\nTier 1: Digital Artifacts\nFormal documents, presentations, financial models, designs.\nUploaded PDF, DOCX, XLSX, SVG, or Figma URL with SHA-256 hash.\nReviewed by Lead Manager against brief; requires explicit approved status.\nTier 2: Field & Telemetry Proof\nProperty site visits, client meetings, facility inspections.\nHardware GPS coordinates (±10m), site photograph with EXIF timestamp.\nGeofence proximity check against verified commercial property coordinates.\nTier 3: Third-Party Confirmations\nLease sign-offs, brokerage payments, member onboarding.\nSigned agreement scan, bank remittance advice, CRM deal transaction ID.\nGeneral Manager and Accounts Manager dual-signature verification.\nTier 4: System Telemetry\nUptime, security scans, server patches, API metrics.\nAutomated Prometheus log, CI/CD run ID, Git commit hash, health probe JSON.\nIT Analyst and Super Admin automated telemetry audit.\n\nEvidence Data Contract Schema:\nJSON Evidence Record Schema\n{\n  \"evidenceId\": \"EVD_20261013_0942\",\n  \"taskId\": \"TSK-084\",\n  \"actorId\": \"CIRIL-EXEC-005\",\n  \"evidenceTier\": 1,\n  \"artifactUri\": \"https://vault.ciril.in/evidence/TSK-084_v2.pdf\",\n  \"sha256\": \"e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855\",\n  \"submittedAt\": \"2026-10-13T10:14:22Z\",\n  \"status\": \"APPROVED\",\n  \"reviewedBy\": \"CIRIL-OPS-004\",\n  \"reviewComments\": \"Proposal structure verified against Bangalore Tech Park RFP.\"\n}\n\n4. Surveillance, Intervention & Escalation Mechanics\nA tracking system is only as effective as its capacity to trigger timely, constructive interventions before operational failures cascade into missed revenue or client loss.\n5.1 The Chairman's Radar vs. General Manager's Detailed Surveillance\nThe system strictly differentiates the surveillance scopes of executive leadership:\nChairman Apex Radar: Displays enterprise-wide health meters, high-level SLA trends, active bottleneck counts, regional deal volumes, and outstanding strategic exceptions. Designed for 10-second cognitive consumption.\nGeneral Manager Surveillance Cockpit: Drills down into individual departments, teams, and employee rosters. Identifies which managers have approval backlogs, which employees have declining completion rates, and which zonal pipelines are lagging.\n\n5.2 Blocker & SLA Breach Severity Matrix\nWhen tasks encounter delays or impediments, they are categorized into four standardized severity tiers defined in iots-system.drawio:\nSeverity Tier\nTrigger Criteria\nRequired Intervention\nEscalation & Notification Path\nCritical (Red)\nSLA missed by >24h, active external blocker on high-value deal, client escalation.\nImmediate emergency meeting; task reassignment or additional resource allocation.\nInstant alert to General Manager & Chairman; notification to Senior Manager.\nHigh (Orange)\nDeadline approaching within 4h with <50% progress; manager review pending >6h.\nLead Manager directly contacts assignee; clears resource roadblocks.\nSenior Operations Manager & Lead Manager dashboard alert.\nMedium (Yellow)\nTask rejected in QA review requiring second revision; minor resource shortage.\nStructured revision cycle with clear written feedback and 24h turn-around.\nLead Operations Manager & Assignee dashboard alert.\nLow (Blue)\nRoutine task running normally; minor progress delay under 2 hours.\nStandard employee progress update and timeline self-correction.\nLogged in employee workbench activity log.\n\n6. Automated Reporting & Objective Recognition Framework\nIOTS eliminates subjective bias by converting verified operational records into automated reports and mathematically transparent employee recognitions.\n6.1 Scheduled Reporting Engines\nDaily Digest (Delivered 19:00): Summarizes today's completed tasks, active blockers, overdue work by owner, team attendance, and top priorities for tomorrow.\nWeekly Performance Scorecard (Delivered Monday 08:30): Cross-team SLA achievement rates, capacity balancing scores, recurring bottlenecks, and regional commercial lead movements.\nMonthly Executive Period Report (Delivered 1st of Month): 30-day productivity trends, verified brokerage collections, 7.5% CIRIL royalties realized, and employee recognition rankings.\n\n6.2 The Performance Reward System (Star Performer Algorithm)\nThe system calculates a monthly Composite Excellence Score for every employee using the formula below:\nComposite Excellence Score Formula\nScore = (0.35 * TCR) + (0.35 * OTDR) + (0.15 * (100 - RCR)) + (0.15 * AttendanceRate)\n\nWhere:\n• TCR = Task Completion Rate (% of assigned work completed)\n• OTDR = On-Time Delivery Rate (% completed on or before due date)\n• RCR = Revision Cycle Rate (% of submissions requiring correction)\n• AttendanceRate = Punctual, verified attendance consistency (% of days present)\n\nQualification Thresholds:\n• Score ≥ 92.0%: Qualifies as 'Star Performer of the Month'.\n• 3 Consecutive Qualifying Months: Automatically escalates to Chairman Cockpit for prestigious Executive Leadership Award and formal compensation appraisal.\n\n7. Database Schema & Telemetry Data Contracts\nTo support this tracking architecture, the backend database implements the Shared Operational Records model specified below:\nTable Entity\nPrimary / Foreign Keys\nCore Telemetry Fields & Invariants\nusers\nPK: empId\nname, email, roleId, permittedRoles (JSON), department, office, availabilityStatus (Available, Meeting, Field, Leave), createdAt.\ntasks\nPK: taskId\nFK: assigneeId, reviewerId\ntitle, description, priority (Low/Med/High/Crit), dueDate, originalDueDate, state (ASSIGNED, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_FOR_REVIEW, UNDER_REVIEW, CLOSED), deliverables.\ntask_activities\nPK: activityId\nFK: taskId, actorId\ntype (NOTE, PROGRESS, TIME, ATTACHMENT), value, effortMinutes, timestamp. Immutable append-only log.\nevidence_records\nPK: evidenceId\nFK: taskId, actorId\ntier (1..4), artifactUri, sha256Hash, submittedAt, status (PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED), reviewedBy, reviewComments.\nattendance_logs\nPK: logId\nFK: empId\ndate, punchInTime, punchOutTime, lat, lon, accuracy, locationStatus (ONSITE, REMOTE), distanceMeters.\ndeals_pipeline\nPK: dealId\nFK: leadGiverId, leadReceiverId\npropertyName, zone, dealValue, brokerageFee, cirilRoyalty (7.5%), status (MANDATE, PROPOSAL, NEGOTIATION, CLOSED), closedAt.\naudit_ledger\nPK: eventId\nFK: actorId\neventType, eventPayload (JSON), ipAddress, userAgent, timestamp. Cryptographically sequenced immutable ledger.\n\nConclusion & Engineering Next Steps:\nThis specification provides the engineering blueprint for connecting the React 19 frontend and Express 5 backend within iots-app. By enforcing immutable evidence collection, continuous telemetry logging, and role-scoped surveillance cockpits, the CIRIL IOTS platform achieves complete operational transparency across the entire organization.\n"}],"isError":false,"_meta":{"codex/nodeReplExecutionDurationMs":123}}

    1. Executive Overview & The 3-Layer Tracking Architecture
    Operational tracking within the Commercial Real Estate Institutional Alliance (CIRIL) is built on an uncompromising principle: Complete Transparency, Absolute Accountability, and Cryptographic Evidence. Large commercial property transactions, inter-city tenant handshakes, and brokerage collections require every team member to operate with military precision.
    Architectural Core Philosophy: Layman Flight Control Center Analogy
    Think of an international airport flight operations center. The Airport Chairman needs a 30-second macro radar showing all flight sectors, delays, and runway safety without baggage-handling details. The General Manager needs detailed operational surveillance over fuel, maintenance, air traffic control, and terminal throughput. Meanwhile, the pilots, ground crew, and mechanics require precision workbenches where every turn of a wrench, inspection report, and pre-flight checklist is logged with immutable proof. IOTS implements this exact paradigm.
    The entire tracking system operates across three synchronized layers defined in iots-system.drawio:
    Layer 1 (Security, Geofencing & Authentication): Hardware GPS perimeter checks, IP address logging, and cryptographically verified employee credentials without public registration. Transparently tags sessions as ONSITE (within 350m of Hyderabad HQ) or REMOTE without disrupting legitimate off-site work.
    Layer 2 (Management, Operations & Execution): Daily work allocation, task lifecycle state transitions, time tracking, live team availability rosters, and the multi-role Evidence Collection Engine. Enforces the golden rule: Work Activity ≠ Task State.
    Layer 3 (Intelligence, Analytics & Reporting): Role-scoped analytics digests, SLA calculation engines, exception/risk radars, commercial 7.5% royalty calculations, and objective employee recognition algorithms (Star Performer of the Month).
    
    2. Core Engineering Invariants & Metric Engine Rules
    To prevent metric corruption, gaming, and artificial workload inflation, the tracking engine enforces five non-negotiable architectural invariants:
    Architectural Invariant
    System-Level Rule
    Engineering Enforcement & Fail-Safe
    Invariant 1: Work Activity ≠ Task State
    Adding notes, effort hours, or uploading attachments are historical activity entries. They NEVER mutate the task status directly.
    Task states (ASSIGNED → IN_PROGRESS → WAITING_FOR_REVIEW → UNDER_REVIEW → CLOSED) can only transition via explicit lifecycle state machine mutations authorized by the assigned actor or manager.
    Invariant 2: Stable Task Identity
    Reassigning or transferring a task never creates a duplicate task entity or resets historical duration.
    The task maintains its unique taskId throughout its entire lifecycle. A ReassignmentRecord is appended preserving original dueDate, prior assignee, and delay history.
    Invariant 3: Zero Denominator Handling
    No metric calculation may divide by zero or emit NaN / null values into executive dashboards.
    If total tasks or denominator is zero, the calculation engine outputs 'N/A' (Not Applicable). If no target is set, outputs 'Target Not Configured' rather than 0%.
    Invariant 4: CRM Financial Boundary
    The external CRM remains the sole authoritative source of truth for commercial deal closing and broker fee totals.
    IOTS imports verified CRM records and strictly tracks internal operational task execution, lead giver (30%) / receiver (70%) follow-ups, and computes CIRIL's 7.5% royalty.
    Invariant 5: Authority Boundary
    Administrative privilege alone does not approve business deliverables, leave requests, or commercial terms.
    Super Admin and IT Analyst control platform infrastructure; business approvals strictly follow configured managerial reporting hierarchies (Lead Manager → Senior Manager → GM).
    
    3. The Universal Evidence System Architecture
    A fundamental requirement of IOTS is that no task can be marked 'Completed' or 'Closed' based on subjective word of mouth. Every operational action requires verifiable evidence. The Evidence System provides four distinct tiers of proof:
    Evidence Tier
    Evidence Classification
    Required Artifact / Payload
    Verification & QA Gate
    Tier 1: Digital Artifacts
    Formal documents, presentations, financial models, designs.
    Uploaded PDF, DOCX, XLSX, SVG, or Figma URL with SHA-256 hash.
    Reviewed by Lead Manager against brief; requires explicit approved status.
    Tier 2: Field & Telemetry Proof
    Property site visits, client meetings, facility inspections.
    Hardware GPS coordinates (±10m), site photograph with EXIF timestamp.
    Geofence proximity check against verified commercial property coordinates.
    Tier 3: Third-Party Confirmations
    Lease sign-offs, brokerage payments, member onboarding.
    Signed agreement scan, bank remittance advice, CRM deal transaction ID.
    General Manager and Accounts Manager dual-signature verification.
    Tier 4: System Telemetry
    Uptime, security scans, server patches, API metrics.
    Automated Prometheus log, CI/CD run ID, Git commit hash, health probe JSON.
    IT Analyst and Super Admin automated telemetry audit.

    # CIRIL Internal Operations Tracking System (IOTS)
    ## Chapter 1: Organizational Roles, Responsibilities & Access Governance
    
    > **Document Code:** `IOTS-DOC-01`  
    > **Target Audience:** All Personnel, Department Heads, System Administrators, and HR Leadership  
    > **Context:** Deconstruction of CIRIL's 11 Institutional Roles, Transition from Single Manager to Distributed Hierarchy, and Real Staff Mappings
    
    ---
    
    ## 1. The Operational Transformation: From Monolith to Distributed Excellence
    
    In earlier operations, CIRIL relied on a heavily centralized managerial bottleneck where a single General Manager / Operations Lead was expected to oversee everything:
    - Coordinating board meetings and minute-taking
    - Chasing member brokerages for deal closures and 7.5% royalty remittances
    - Running cold calls and member expansion outreach
    - Overseeing social media posts and graphic design proofreading
    - Calling vendors for conference stationery and report printing
    - Managing day-to-day employee leaves, attendance, and task status
    
    This bottleneck created severe operational risks: single points of failure, delayed task reviews, employee burnout, and limited real-time visibility for the Chairman.
    
    The **Internal Operations Tracking System (IOTS)** redesigns CIRIL’s operational hierarchy into **11 clearly bounded roles**. It establishes a clear operational chain of command where:
    1. Executive strategy is held by the **Chairman**.
    2. Platform integrity and technical diagnostics are safeguarded by **Super Admin** and the **IT System Analyst** (both possessing equal system-level privileges).
    3. Routine organizational housekeeping is managed by the **Admin**.
    4. Management is distributed across three focused tiers: **General Manager**, **Senior Manager**, and **Lead Manager**.
    5. Execution is handled by dedicated specialists: **Executive**, **Business Development Executive (BDE)**, **Social Media Manager**, and **Graphic Designer**.
    
    ---
    
    ## 2. Institutional Hierarchy & Organizational Chain of Command
    
    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
        Chairman["1. Chairman\n(Apex Executive Oversight & Strategic Radar)"]
        
        subgraph PlatformTech ["Platform Governance & Technical Command (Co-Equal Privileges)"]
            SuperAdmin["2. Super Admin\n(Policy, RBAC, Platform Authority)"]
            ITAnalyst["4. IT System Analyst\n(Health, APIs, Security Diagnostics)"]
        end
        
        Admin["3. Admin\n(User Onboarding, Geofences, Routine Administration)"]
        
        subgraph ManagementTier ["Management Tier (Distributed Leadership)"]
            GM["5. General Manager\n(Governance, Finance, Legal & Expansion Oversight)"]
            SM["6. Senior Manager\n(Multi-Team Operations, Workload Balancing & SLA Delivery)"]
            LM["7. Lead Manager\n(Team Command, Daily Task Assignment & QA Approvals)"]
        end
        
        subgraph ExecutionTier ["Execution Tier (Specialized Execution Workbenches)"]
            Exec["8. Executive\n(Operations & Vertical Delivery)"]
            BDE["9. Business Development Executive\n(Membership Outreach & Prospecting)"]
            SMM["10. Social Media Manager\n(Campaigns & Content Calendar)"]
            GD["11. Graphic Designer\n(Creative Collaterals & Version Assets)"]
        end
    
        Chairman -.-> SuperAdmin
        Chairman -.-> GM
        SuperAdmin <==> ITAnalyst
        SuperAdmin --> Admin
        GM --> SM
        SM --> LM
        LM --> Exec
        LM --> BDE
        LM --> SMM
        LM --> GD
    ```
    
    ---
    
    ## 3. Exhaustive Role Breakdown & CIRIL Staff Mapping
    
    ### Role 1: Chairman
    - **Layman's Analogy:** The Captain on the bridge of a naval ship. The Captain does not grease the engines or peel vegetables, but continuously watches the global radar, verifies heading and fuel, and steps in when high-risk hazards appear.
    - **Operational Scope:** Entire Enterprise (National Headquarters, All Geographic Zones, All Functional Departments).
    - **Real CIRIL Function:**
      - Receives complete bird's-eye operational intelligence across the entire alliance.
      - Monitors high-level commercial deal flow and royalty collections (ensuring CIRIL’s 7.5% royalty health).
      - Inspects company-wide attendance and location audit summaries, specifically tracking remote/unknown location trends.
      - Reviews the **Executive "Requires Attention" Cockpit**: overdue task clusters, repeated task reassignments, and unresolved departmental blockers.
      - Reviews the **Quarterly Reward & Recognition Standings** to personally sign off on the 3-consecutive-month excellence commendations.
    - **Permitted Actions:**
      - View all organizational metrics, departments, teams, tasks, and audit logs.
      - Issue high-priority executive directives or escalations (requires secondary confirmation).
      - Publish enterprise-wide Chairman Announcements.
    - **Forbidden Actions:**
      - Cannot reset routine employee passwords (delegated to Admin).
      - Cannot perform everyday task reassignment or micro-manage task checklists.
    
    ---
    
    ### Role 2: Super Admin
    - **Layman's Analogy:** The Chief Architect and Master Key Holder of a skyscraper. They configure the master security doors, define who can enter which floor, and oversee system safety.
    - **Operational Scope:** System-Wide Platform Architecture.
    - **System Parity Note:** **Super Admin and IT System Analyst have equal platform privileges.** The Super Admin focuses on administrative governance, while the IT Analyst focuses on technical infrastructure.
    - **Key Responsibilities:**
      - Manages master organizational configurations, department definitions, and role definitions.
      - Configures Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) permission sets.
      - Holds authority to deactivate or alter high-level accounts.
      - Inspects full, immutable system audit logs.
      - Manages data export covenants and compliance frameworks.
    - **Permitted Actions:**
      - Full read/write/configure access across all database tables, user records, and operational settings.
      - Grant or revoke user roles and multi-role assignments.
      - Define custom geofence boundaries for official offices.
    
    ---
    
    ### Role 3: Admin
    - **Layman's Analogy:** The Facility Operations Manager of a corporate campus. They issue employee ID cards, set office opening hours, maintain the company directory, and announce building updates.
    - **Operational Scope:** Routine Organizational Administration & Operations Support.
    - **Key Responsibilities:**
      - **Structured User Provisioning:** Manually creates internal user profiles (Employee ID, Designation, Department, Office Location, System Role, Reporting Manager). *There is no public registration.*
      - **Location & Geofence Perimeter Management:** Configures approved office GPS coordinates and allowable radius boundaries (e.g., 100 meters).
      - **Attendance Auditing:** Reviews location exceptions, off-site attendance flags, and unexcused late arrivals.
      - **Global Task Oversight:** Monitors organizational work queues to identify abandoned tasks or perform archival cleanups.
      - **Company Announcements:** Drafts and publishes official communications to specific teams or the entire organization.
    - **Permitted Actions:**
      - Create and edit user profiles, activate/deactivate accounts, trigger password recovery workflows.
      - Manage office location boundaries and view location audit logs.
      - Archive completed operational records upon administrative approval.
    - **Forbidden Actions:**
      - Cannot alter core code, platform security schemas, or system API connections (restricted to Super Admin & IT Analyst).
    
    ---
    
    ### Role 4: IT System Analyst
    - **Layman's Analogy:** The Chief Flight Engineer monitoring engine temperatures, avionics, electrical bus lines, and fuel injection systems.
    - **Operational Scope:** Technical Reliability, API Ecosystem, Security Diagnostics & Infrastructure.
    - **System Parity Note:** **Possesses equal system privileges with Super Admin.** Tailored for real-time technical monitoring and diagnostic intervention.
    - **Key Responsibilities:**
      - **Application & Service Health:** Continuously monitors server uptime, database response latency, and WebGL/frontend performance.
      - **External API Integrations:** Tracks status and rate-limits of external services (e.g., BigDataCloud reverse geocoding, mail servers, storage buckets).
      - **Authentication & Security Auditing:** Analyzes anomalous login attempts, sudden location jumps (impossible travel velocity), and session timeouts.
      - **Technical Incident Response:** Logs and resolves platform bugs, database deadlocks, or webhook delivery failures.
      - **Deployment Tracking:** Logs system version updates, environment variable changes, and schema migrations.
    - **Permitted Actions:**
      - Full system-level diagnostics, raw audit log exploration, session invalidation, and database maintenance.
      - Full technical configuration parity with Super Admin.
    - **Forbidden Actions:**

    ### Role 5: General Manager (CIRIL Staff Mapping: Ipsheeta)

      - **Cross-Functional Escalation Resolution:** Acts as the senior escalation clearinghouse when disputes arise between member offices or functional teams.
    - **Permitted Actions:**
      - Cross-departmental task visibility, high-level approval of budgets, leave approvals for managers, resolution of escalated blockers.
    - **Forbidden Actions:**
      - Cannot edit underlying software configuration or change database schemas.
    
    ---
    
    ### Role 6: Senior Manager
    - **Layman's Analogy:** The Division Superintendent who oversees multiple project foremen, ensuring that all teams move at the same speed and no single crew is overwhelmed.
    - **Operational Scope:** Multi-Team Supervision, Delivery Assurance, and Workload Balancing.
    - **Key Responsibilities:**
      - **Cross-Team Workload Balancing:** Monitors workload distribution across operational teams (e.g., Operations Team, BD Team, Creative Team), shifting tasks if one team is overloaded.
      - **SLA & Deadline Risk Mitigation:** Identifies tasks at risk of missing client or member deadlines across multiple verticals.
      - **Manager Approval Queue:** Evaluates high-impact decisions escalated by Lead Managers (e.g., significant deadline extensions, repeated reassignments).
      - **Performance Comparison:** Analyzes comparative productivity trends between teams to address operational bottlenecks.
    - **Permitted Actions:**
      - Reallocate work between different teams or lead managers.
      - Intervene in overdue or blocked tasks that exceed team-level authority.
      - Authorize second-tier approvals for operational requests.

        children.push(h1('6. Role workspaces and tracking specification'));
        children.push(p('The following are dashboard requirements, not assertions that the features already exist. The workspace resolver uses the authenticated employee’s assigned workspace and permissions. The Creatives Communication Associate is one IOTS role with two functional views (design and social distribution).'));
        for (const r of roles) {

          children.push(label('Purpose:',r.purpose));
          children.push(h3('Dashboard panels'));
          for (const [a,b] of r.panels) children.push(bullet(a+' — '+b));
          children.push(h3('Measures and calculation rules'));
          children.push(metricRows(r.metrics));
          children.push(p('Targets: Not set unless explicitly approved in versioned configuration. Do not copy target values from Gemini or other draft documents into production. Every percent follows the sample-size and denominator rules in Section 2.',{spacing:{before:100,after:80}}));
          children.push(h3('Scope and actions'));
          children.push(label('Can see / do:',r.scope));
          children.push(label('Alerts:',r.alerts));
          children.push(label('Evidence:',r.evidence));
          children.push(h3('Panel API and example response'));
          children.push(p(r.api));

          children.push(h3('Additional data needed'));
          children.push(p(r.data));
        }
        
        children.push(h1('7. Risk flags and routing'));
        children.push(p('Risk flags should explain an observed condition and point to the person with the configured authority to act. A flag is not a performance verdict. The backend stores the rule version, observed values, creation time, assigned decision role, action, reason, and clearing event. Severity thresholds and routing are configuration, not constants. Confirm whether the system uses Low/Medium/High or adds Critical.'));
        children.push(table(['Rule example','Evidence and measure','Default destination to configure','Clear condition'],[
        ['Overdue work','Task due-date history, state, age bucket, owner, current reviewer.','Lead Manager; Senior Manager for cross-team/high-impact; GM/Chairman summary by severity.','Closed, approved extension, or explicit cancellation.'],
        ['Due soon without update','Due date, required-update rule, qualifying activity age.','Lead Manager and assignee.','Qualifying update or state transition.'],
        ['Review waiting','Submission time, reviewer mandate, business-hour age.','Assigned reviewer’s manager; senior route if configured wait limit exceeded.','Decision recorded.'],
        ['Repeated transfers','Transfer count, reasons, original owner and overdue history.','Senior Manager; GM summary for cross-team pattern.','Reasoned decision and next owner/action recorded.'],
        ['Open blocker','Blocker severity, age, external/internal label, business impact and evidence.','Owner role based on impact and mandate; Chairman sees only material summary.','Resolution verified or accepted mitigation/monitoring decision.'],
        ['Evidence rejected repeatedly','Checklist, evidence versions and review reasons.','Assignee and reviewer; manager for repeated failure.','Required evidence accepted or task cancelled through formal decision.'],
        ['Attendance exception','Expected schedule, punch events, approved leave and correction history.','Employee and Admin; manager only per mandate.','Correction/decision recorded with reason.'],
        ['Unknown location repeated','Only explicit login/check-in/field checks, accuracy and device/source context allowed by policy.','Admin or security-authorised role; escalation by configured threshold.','Reviewed decision; never auto-label as misconduct.'],
        ['Request pending too long','Request time, type, business-hour clock, return-for-detail pauses.','Configured approver and their escalation role.','Decision or documented return-for-detail.'],
        ['Overload','Estimate-based planned hours vs scheduled capacity with data coverage.','Lead Manager; Senior Manager if cross-team.','Capacity decision or period ends; retain decision trail.'],
        ['Royalty mismatch / stale CRM','CRM source, split version, expected and verified amounts, sync time.','Configured finance/reconciliation authority; GM summary; Chairman material summary.','Reconciled or documented dispute.'],
        ['Authentication anomaly','Rate-limited auth events, impossible-travel rule only if approved, account/session references.','IT/security role; account action by configured authority.','Incident decision and mitigation recorded.']],[1850,3200,2450,1560]));
        children.push(h2('Risk record and alert card'));
        children.push(code('{ riskId, ruleId, ruleVersion, severity, observedAt, scopeRef, subjectRef, evidenceRefs[], observedValues, reasonText, nextRole, assignedTo, decisionDueAt, status, decisionRef, clearCondition, clearedAt }'));
        children.push(p('A dashboard alert should state: “what happened”, “why it was flagged”, “what record proves it”, “who owns the next decision”, and “what clears it”. Never label an employee as risky or underperforming from an unreviewed automated signal.'));
        
        children.push(h1('8. Data model additions and minimum field needs'));
        children.push(p('These are design fields needed to support the measures and history. Fit them into the selected database model after the schema and migrations are agreed. Preserve append-only history for event records; use effective-dated versions for rules and configuration.'));
        children.push(table(['Record group','Fields needed beyond a simple task/user table','Why'],[
        ['Role and permission','roleAssignmentId, employeeId, roleId, scopeRefs, mandateId, validFrom/To, grantedBy, reason, reviewedAt, permissionVersion.','Multi-role identity, server-side scope and configured approval authority.'],
        ['Task and assignment','originalDueAt, currentDueAt/version, estimateMinutes, firstSubmittedAt, cancelledAt/reason, dueDateChange history, assigned/reviewer history, task type, checklist template/version.','Correct workload and fairness calculations; stable task ID.'],
        ['Task event/activity','eventId, taskId, actorId, activeRole, eventType, occurredAt, recordedAt, payload, source/correlation ID.','Separate work activity from formal state transitions and reconstruct history.'],
        ['Review/submission','submissionId/version, submittedAt, submitter, reviewer assignment, decision/status, decidedAt, business-hours duration, reason, authority mandate.','On-time at submission; review latency and first-time acceptance.'],
        ['Evidence/checklist','evidence fields in Section 4; checklist item type/required flag; accepted/rejected decision and supersedes link.','Enforce submission and closure gates; preserve rejected versions.'],
        ['Attendance/schedule','scheduleId/version, local timezone, scheduled start/end, grace rule version, punch event IDs, source and accuracy, location tag, correction link/reason.','Attendance and punctuality denominator; transparent correction handling.'],
        ['Leave/availability','request type/state history, approved interval, decision actor/mandate/reason; availability events with start/end and source.','Fair exclusions and current availability with freshness.'],
        ['Issue/escalation','issue type, task link, opened/resolved times, internal/external context, impact, severity, owner role, routing, decision and clear condition.','Blocker age, risk rules and accountable action.'],
        ['Metric/rule/target','metricDefinitionId/version, formula version, target nullable, minimum sample, calendar/period, effective dates, scope, exclusion rules, approver.','Reproducible results and no silently retroactive policy change.'],
        ['CRM/royalty','CRM source ID, sync version/time/status, party brokerage shares, split authority/version, royalty rate/version, due/collected allocation, payment proof, reconciliation state.','Keep CRM authoritative and show provisional vs verified totals.'],
        ['Governance/content','obligation type, owner, due date, state, external reference/evidence, source freshness; announcement audience/delivery events.','GM governance panels and admin announcement tracking.'],
        ['System telemetry','service/environment, probe time/result, route group, sample coverage, incident IDs/timeline, deploy/migration version/checksum/outcome/recovery reference.','IT dashboard and operational reliability.'],
        ['Audit/export','actor, activeRole, action, entity ref, before/after or safe diff, timestamp, request ID, purpose, scope, export artifact hash/ref, integrity-check status.','Accountability for sensitive reads, changes and exports.']],[1900,4800,2360]));
        
        children.push(h1('9. Reports and recognition'));
        children.push(h2('Reports'));
        children.push(p('Provide daily, weekly and monthly reports per recipient and permission scope. Schedule and delivery channel are Not set until approved. Each report states period, as-of time, metric definition versions, missing-source coverage, and links to source records. Report generation and export are audit events. Daily report can summarize completions, due/overdue work, blockers, attendance exceptions, and next-day priorities. Weekly report can compare team delivery and workload with sample sizes. Monthly report can show metric history, verified royalty reconciliation, and recognition eligibility.'));
        children.push(h2('Recognition'));
        children.push(p('Keep eligibility separate from ranking. The draft qualification values (completion above 90%, on-time above 90%, revision below 10%, attendance above 95%, minimum task count, and three consecutive qualifying months) are proposed examples only. Store thresholds, exclusions, minimum sample, metric versions, weights and approver in configuration. Until approved, show “Recognition rules not configured” and do not rank employees.'));
        children.push(p('If approved, calculate qualification from verified records for a closed period, preserve the exact inputs and rule version, and produce an evidence pack. Missing denominator, inadequate sample, incomplete attendance schedule, or stale source data makes the criterion “insufficient data”, not zero or automatic failure. Three consecutive qualifying periods create a Chairman review item only if that authority is confirmed. The final decision and reason are appended.'));
        
        children.push(h1('10. Decisions required before implementation'));
        children.push(table(['Decision','Why it is needed','Safe draft behavior until decided'],[

        ['Approval mandates and scope','Title alone must not grant approval.','Return only server-configured scopes; deny decision actions without mandate.'],
        ['Metric periods and calendars','Office timezone, workdays, holidays and business-hour rules affect denominators and latency.','Show timezone and period; mark unavailable where calendar is missing.'],
        ['Targets and sample minimum','Several draft values conflict or are unapproved.','Targets show “Not configured”; proposed minimum sample 5 must be approved/configured.'],
        ['Extension and transfer attribution','Needed to fairly assign due work and ownership history.','Preserve all owners and dates; show unassigned attribution as unresolved until policy.'],

        ['CRM integration and royalty math','CRM is financial truth; brokerage split source and royalty calculation basis need confirmation.','Display provisional/unreconciled values; do not assume 30/70 shares or treat 7.5% as approved if absent from policy.'],

        ['API/session/database and hosting','Required for implementation; integration plan flags session uncertainty.','Agree contract, secure session, database, migrations, environment and audit model before wiring.'],
        ['Monitoring service objectives','Uptime, latency and alert targets are unspecified.','Show coverage and measured values; label SLO target as not configured.']],[2500,3650,2910]));
        
        children.push(h1('11. Recommended build order'));
        children.push(p('Build the records where work begins first, then the management views that consume those records. Each phase ends with a working frontend-to-API path, authorised source drilldown, and tests of both success and failure paths.'));
        const phases=[
        ['0. Confirm policy and contract','Confirm role mapping, authority mandates, target ownership, calendars, retention, evidence types, CRM fields and session/database choices. Freeze API response/error envelope and initial schema.','Approved decision log; sample records; permission matrix.'],
        ['1. Shared foundation','Implement API entry point, session/role context, migrations, append-only audit/event model, health check, Vite proxy and test seed.','Both apps run locally; API health reachable through frontend proxy; no real secrets in seed.'],
        ['2. Executive personal workbench','Implement task list/detail, activities, estimates, evidence checklist, submission gates, attendance/request self-service and personal metrics.','One task can be assigned, worked, submitted and traced as one ID; user sees only own data.'],
        ['3. Lead Manager workbench','Add team scope, allocation, review queue, evidence acceptance, reasons, requests and transfer/extension history.','Reviewer distinct from submitter; transition/evidence gates enforced by API; review time captured.'],
        ['4. Add BDE and Creatives work creation','Implement outreach/follow-up/handoff and asset/version/publication records; connect CRM references without duplicating financial truth.','Source IDs, freshness, attribution and proof available for later management rollups.'],
