     ]}/></Panel><Panel title="Recovery readiness"><div className="check-list"><p><Check size={17}/> Backup completed · 13 Oct 02:00 IST</p><p><Check size={17}/> Restore exercise · 10 Oct · verified</p><p><Clock size={17}/> Recovery time / data-loss targets: Not set</p><p><ShieldCheck size={17}/> File scanning: 12 of 12 demo files clean</p></div></Panel></div><Panel title="Incidents and authentication anomalies"><Table rows={data.issues.filter(i=>i.id.startsWith('INC'))} columns={[
     ['Incident',r=><strong>{r.id} · {r.title}</strong>],['Owner',r=>person(r.owner)],['State',r=><Badge>{r.status}</Badge>],['Recovery step',r=>r.resolution],['Action',r=><Button onClick={()=>{setNote('');setDetail({kind:'incident',id:r.id})}}>Record resolution</Button>]
     ]}/><div className="panel-foot">AUTH-017 · 8 failed sign-ins in 10 minutes · E10 assigned · Review source logs; no automatic employee judgement.</div></Panel><Panel title="Deployment and migration records"><Table rows={[{id:'DEP-024',release:'demo-1.4.2',at:'12 Oct, 18:00 IST',result:'Verified',proof:'Health checks passed; rollback package retained'},{id:'MIG-008',release:'evidence_version_index',at:'12 Oct, 17:45 IST',result:'Verified',proof:'Counts reconciled; restore point BACKUP-012'}]} columns={['Record','Release / migration','Time','Outcome','Evidence'].map((l,i)=>[l,r=>[r.id,r.release,r.at,<Badge>{r.result}</Badge>,r.proof][i]])}/></Panel></>}
     function toolbar(options=states){return <div className="toolbar"><label className="search"><Search size={17}/><input aria-label="Search records" placeholder="Search name, record or linked entity…" value={query} onChange={e=>setQuery(e.target.value)}/></label><select aria-label="Filter records" value={filter} onChange={e=>setFilter(e.target.value)}><option>All</option>{options.map(o=><option key={o}>{o}</option>)}</select><span className="muted">{teamRole?'Assigned scope':'Own records'}</span></div>}
     function reports(){const fields={Employee:directory.map(e=>e.name),Manager:[...new Set(directory.map(e=>person(e.manager)))],Team:[...new Set(directory.map(e=>e.team))],Role:[...new Set(directory.map(e=>e.role))],Department:[...new Set(directory.map(e=>e.team))],Branch:[...new Set(directory.map(e=>e.branch))],Priority:['High','Normal'],Status:states,Request:['Pending','Approved','Rejected'],Attendance:availability,Risk:['High','Medium','No active flag']}; const rows=mine.filter(t=>{const e=employees.find(e=>e.id===t.owner),r=flags(data,[t.owner]).filter(r=>r.source===t.id),a=data.attendance.find(a=>a.employee===t.owner);return Object.entries(reportFilters).every(([k,v])=>!v||({Employee:e.name,Manager:person(e.manager),Team:e.team,Role:e.role,Department:e.team,Branch:e.branch,Priority:t.priority,Status:t.state,Attendance:a?.status,Risk:r[0]?.severity||'No active flag',Request:data.requests.find(x=>x.owner===t.owner)?.status}[k]===v))}).filter(t=>{const [s,e]=bounds(period);return new Date(t.due)>=s&&new Date(t.due)<=e});
     const exportReport=()=>{if(reportFormat==='PDF'){window.print();notify('Use Save as PDF in the print dialog.');return;}if(reportFormat==='Dashboard'){notify('Filtered dashboard preview updated below.');return;}if(reportFormat==='Authorised email'){update(d=>d.reports.unshift({id:'REP-'+(d.reports.length+1),format:reportFormat,records:rows.length,recipient:person(reportRecipient),status:'Simulated delivery · no email sent'}),'Report email simulated','REPORT-DEMO');notify('Simulated delivery saved. No external email was sent.');return;}const output=rows.map(t=>({'Task ID':t.id,Task:t.title,Employee:person(t.owner),State:t.state,Entity:t.entity,'Original deadline':t.originalDue,'Approved deadline':t.due,'First submission':t.firstSubmitted||'Not recorded',Context:t.exclusion||'None','Data as of':ASOF,'Definition version':'1'}));const book=XLSX.utils.book_new();XLSX.utils.book_append_sheet(book,XLSX.utils.json_to_sheet(output),'Work records');if(reportFormat==='Appraisal template')XLSX.utils.book_append_sheet(book,XLSX.utils.json_to_sheet([{Employee:me.name,Period:period,'Work evidence':'See Work records','Manager feedback':'To be completed','Employee response':'To be completed','Decision':'Human review required'}]),'Appraisal');XLSX.writeFile(book,`IOTS-${role.key}-${reportFormat==='Appraisal template'?'appraisal':'report'}.xlsx`);update(d=>d.reports.unshift({id:'REP-'+(d.reports.length+1),format:reportFormat,records:rows.length,recipient:me.name,status:'Exported'}),'Report exported','REPORT-DEMO');notify('Excel report generated with source records.');};
     return <><Panel title="Build a scoped report" subtitle="All filters combine. Reporting period follows the page selector."><div className="report-filters">{Object.entries(fields).map(([k,values])=><Field key={k} label={k}><select value={reportFilters[k]||''} onChange={e=>setReportFilters({...reportFilters,[k]:e.target.value})}><option value="">All {k.toLowerCase()} values</option>{values.map(v=><option key={v}>{v}</option>)}</select></Field>)}</div><div className="inset actions"><Field label="Output"><select value={reportFormat} onChange={e=>setReportFormat(e.target.value)}>{['Dashboard','PDF','Excel','Authorised email','Appraisal template'].map(f=><option key={f}>{f}</option>)}</select></Field>{reportFormat==='Authorised email'&&<Field label="Authorised demo recipient"><select value={reportRecipient} onChange={e=>setReportRecipient(e.target.value)}>{directory.map(e=><option key={e.id} value={e.id}>{e.name}</option>)}</select></Field>}<Button primary icon={Download} onClick={exportReport}>Generate report</Button><Button onClick={()=>setReportFilters({})}>Clear filters</Button></div></Panel><Panel title={`${rows.length} matching work records`} subtitle={`${period} · ${role.label} assigned scope · definition v1`}><Table rows={rows} columns={taskColumns}/></Panel><Panel title="Report jobs"><Table rows={data.reports.filter(r=>r.recipient===me.name||teamRole)} columns={['ID','Output','Records','Recipient','Status'].map((l,i)=>[l,r=>[r.id,r.format,r.records,r.recipient,r.status][i]])}/></Panel></>}
     function content(){switch(view){
     case 'overview':return overview();
     case 'tasks':return <>{toolbar([...states,'Overdue','Due soon','External blocker'])}<Panel title="Work register" subtitle="Activity updates do not change task state. Open a task to view evidence and decisions."><Table rows={mine.filter(match).filter(t=>filter==='All'||t.state===filter||filter==='Overdue'&&isOverdue(t)||filter==='External blocker'&&t.blocker||filter==='Due soon'&&active(t)&&new Date(t.due)>new Date(ASOF)&&new Date(t.due)-new Date(ASOF)<data.config.dueSoonDays*86400000)} columns={taskColumns}/></Panel><Panel title="Transfers and ownership history">{transferTable()}</Panel></>;
     case 'people':return <>{toolbar(availability)}<Panel title="Employee monitor" subtitle="Open an employee for work, attendance, blockers, review delays and feedback.">{filter==='All'?employeeTable():<Table rows={directory.filter(e=>data.attendance.find(a=>a.employee===e.id)?.status===filter).filter(match)} columns={[['Employee',e=><LinkButton onClick={()=>setDetail({kind:'employee',id:e.id})}>{e.name}</LinkButton>],['Availability',e=><Badge>{filter}</Badge>],['Team',e=>e.team]]}/>}</Panel>{teamRole&&<div className="grid two"><Panel title="Team comparison">{teamComparison()}</Panel><Panel title="Feedback and evaluation">{feedbackView()}</Panel></div>}</>;
     case 'attendance':{const own=data.attendance.find(a=>a.employee===role.employee);return <><div className="section-note"><CalendarDays size={18}/><span>Complete records determine working hours. Leave and incomplete records keep their context. Location is recorded only at explicit events.</span></div><Panel title="My attendance controls"><div className="inset actions"><Field label="Availability"><select value={own.status} onChange={e=>update(d=>{d.attendance.find(a=>a.employee===role.employee).status=e.target.value},'Availability changed',own.id,e.target.value)}>{availability.map(s=><option key={s}>{s}</option>)}</select></Field><Button disabled={!!own.out} onClick={()=>{update(d=>{const a=d.attendance.find(a=>a.employee===role.employee);a.breaks+=15;a.status='On Break'},'Break recorded',own.id,'15-minute demo break');notify('15-minute demo break recorded.')}}>Record 15-minute break</Button><Button primary disabled={!own.in||!!own.out} onClick={()=>{update(d=>{const a=d.attendance.find(a=>a.employee===role.employee);a.out=ASOF;a.status='Offline'},'Checked out',own.id);notify('Demo checkout recorded; complete hours calculated.')}}>Check out</Button></div></Panel><Panel title="Daily attendance" subtitle="13 Oct · 09:00 proposed start · lateness policy not configured">{attendanceTable(data.attendance.filter(a=>role.key==='admin'||ids.includes(a.employee)))}</Panel><Panel title="Attendance measures"><div className="inset"><p><b>Attendance / punctuality:</b> N/A — the prototype has one current-day record per employee; a complete scheduled-day denominator and holiday calendar are not configured.</p><p><b>Late and absence comparison:</b> Not available for prior periods. Approved leave is kept visible and excluded from eligible days.</p><LinkButton onClick={()=>setView('requests')}>Request a correction with supporting evidence</LinkButton></div></Panel></>}
     case 'requests':return <><div className="grid two wide-left"><Panel title="Requests and decisions" subtitle="A named mandate determines who can decide."><Table rows={data.requests.filter(r=>ids.includes(r.owner)||r.approver===role.employee)} columns={[
     ['Request',r=><><strong>{r.type}</strong><small>{r.id} · {person(r.owner)}</small></>],['Source / reason',r=><><LinkButton onClick={()=>linkTask(r.task)}>{r.task}</LinkButton><small>{r.reason}</small></>],['Decision',r=><Badge>{r.status}</Badge>],['Mandated reviewer',r=><>{person(r.approver)}{r.status==='Pending'&&r.approver===role.employee&&<Button onClick={()=>{setNote('');setDetail({kind:'request',id:r.id})}}>Review request</Button>}</>]
     ]}/></Panel><Panel title="Make a request"><div className="inset"><Field label="Request type"><select value={requestType} onChange={e=>setRequestType(e.target.value)}>{['Deadline extension','Leave','Attendance correction','Access change','Work blocker'].map(s=><option key={s}>{s}</option>)}</select></Field><Field label="Linked work record"><select value={requestSource} onChange={e=>setRequestSource(e.target.value)}><option value="">Choose a record</option>{work.map(t=><option key={t.id} value={t.id}>{t.id} · {t.title}</option>)}<option value={'ATT-'+role.employee}>My attendance</option></select></Field><Field label="Reason and evidence reference"><textarea value={note} onChange={e=>setNote(e.target.value)}/></Field><Button primary disabled={!note.trim()||!requestSource} onClick={()=>{update(d=>d.requests.unshift({id:'REQ-'+(100+d.requests.length),type:requestType,owner:role.employee,task:requestSource,status:'Pending',reason:note,created:ASOF,approver:requestType==='Attendance correction'?'E08':'E04'}),'Request submitted',requestSource,note);setNote('');notify('Request saved for the configured demo reviewer.')}}>Submit request</Button></div></Panel></div><Panel title="Issues and escalations"><Table rows={data.issues.filter(i=>teamRole||i.owner===role.employee||mine.some(t=>t.id===i.source))} columns={[
     ['Issue',i=><>{i.title}<small>{i.id} · {i.source}</small></>],['Owner',i=>person(i.owner)],['State',i=><Badge>{i.status}</Badge>],['Next action',i=>i.resolution],['Decision',i=><Button onClick={()=>{setNote('');setDetail({kind:'incident',id:i.id})}} disabled={i.owner!==role.employee}>Record outcome</Button>]
     ]}/></Panel>{attentionPanel()}</>;
     case 'evidence':return <>{toolbar(['Submitted','Accepted','Rejected','Superseded','Missing'])}<Panel title="Evidence register" subtitle="Version history remains visible. Required items need independent acceptance."><Table rows={mine.flatMap(t=>t.evidence.map(e=>({...e,task:t.id}))).filter(match).filter(e=>filter==='All'||e.status===filter)} columns={[
     ['Evidence',e=><>{e.name}<small>{e.id} · v{e.version}</small></>],['Task / type',e=><><LinkButton onClick={()=>linkTask(e.task)}>{e.task}</LinkButton><small>{e.type}</small></>],['Status',e=><Badge>{e.status}</Badge>],['Submitted / reviewed',e=><>{person(e.submitter)}<small>{e.reviewer?person(e.reviewer):'Independent review pending'}</small></>],['Decision reason',e=>e.reason]
     ]}/></Panel><Panel title="Evidence coverage"><div className="inset"><p>Supported design types: work artifact, location proof, external confirmation, outreach log, publication proof, system record and decision record.</p><p>Files in this prototype are simulated references. Production needs versioned storage, actual SHA-256 hashes, file scanning, retention rules and access checks before download.</p></div></Panel></>;
     case 'membership':return <>{toolbar(['Research','Outreach','Response / follow-up','GM meeting','Agreement / fees','Review outcome'])}{membershipPanel()}<Panel title="Prospect follow-up">{filter==='All'?prospectTable():<Table rows={scopedProspects.filter(p=>p.stage===filter).filter(match)} columns={[['Prospect',p=>p.name],['Stage',p=>p.stage],['Next follow-up',p=>niceDate(p.next)]]}/>}</Panel><Panel title="Member directory" subtitle="Firm, city and zone only. Operational activity elsewhere is fictional."><Table rows={members.filter(match)} columns={[
     ['Member firm',m=>m.firm],['City',m=>m.city],['Zone',m=>m.zone],['Directory reference',m=>m.id]
     ]}/></Panel></>;
     case 'deals':return <>{royaltyPanel()}<Panel title="Lead to royalty register" subtitle="CRM owns financial amounts. Source shares must be confirmed per agreement."><Table rows={scopedDeals} columns={[
     ['Requirement',d=><><LinkButton onClick={()=>setDetail({kind:'deal',id:d.id})}>{d.client}</LinkButton><small>{d.id} · {d.city} · {d.area}</small></>],['Member handoff',d=><>{members.find(m=>m.id===d.giver)?.firm}<small>to {members.find(m=>m.id===d.receiver)?.firm}</small></>],['Stage',d=><Badge>{d.stage}</Badge>],['Owner',d=>person(d.owner)],['Due / collected',d=><>{d.brokerage?money(d.brokerage*.075):'Not yet due'}<small>{money(d.collected)} verified</small></>]
     ]}/></Panel><Panel title="Workflow and decision outcomes"><div className="inset"><div className="step-track">{['CRM lead','Member decision','Proposal','Negotiation','Concluded','Brokerage accepted','Royalty verified'].map(s=><span key={s}>{s}</span>)}</div><p><b>Member accepts:</b> assign the local receiver and dated proposal task. <b>Member declines:</b> keep the reason and route back to HQ for another receiver. <b>Payment unverified:</b> retain the outstanding amount and dated follow-up.</p><p>Demo split 30 / 70 is an agreement example, not a universal CIRIL rule.</p></div></Panel></>;
     case 'creative':return <>{creativePanel()}<Panel title="Design and social publishing"><Table rows={[{id:'CAM-014',name:'Quarterly market report',channel:'PDF / member circulation',due:'15 Oct',status:'Waiting for Review',proof:'Artwork v2.0 + proofreading checklist'},{id:'CAM-015',name:'Member spotlight: southern region',channel:'LinkedIn',due:'16 Oct',status:'Assigned',proof:'Publication URL not yet available'},{id:'CAM-016',name:'Regional meeting invitation',channel:'Print + email',due:'19 Oct',status:'In Progress',proof:'Print-ready PDF checklist pending'}]} columns={['Asset','Channel','Publish date','State','Evidence'].map((l,i)=>[l,r=>[r.name,r.channel,r.due,<Badge>{r.status}</Badge>,r.proof][i]])}/></Panel><Panel title="Creative measures"><div className="inset"><p>First-submission on-time and revision rates use the work register above. Publication proof: <b>0 of 1</b> scheduled approved publications in this sample. Proofreading turnaround: <b>N/A</b> until the review closes.</p><p>Engagement: <b>Target not configured</b>. Sample reach and likes are not used to rate employee performance. Inbound enquiries route to the assigned BDE with an acknowledgement record.</p></div></Panel></>;
     case 'governance':return <><Panel title="Governance register">{governanceTable()}</Panel><Panel title="Review and evidence"><div className="inset"><p>Board decisions link minutes, named owners and dates. Filings retain receipt references. Agreements require the signed version. Invoices reference CRM and finance verification; IOTS does not replace accounting.</p></div></Panel></>;
     case 'recognition':return <Panel title="Recognition review" subtitle="Qualification is a review input, not an automatic award."><div className="section-note"><AlertTriangle size={18}/><span>Minimum task count and scoring weights are <b>Not set</b>. Ranking and qualification are unavailable.</span></div><Table rows={employees.filter(e=>['E05','E06','E07'].includes(e.id))} columns={[
     ['Employee',e=>e.name],['Three-month evidence',e=><LinkButton onClick={()=>setDetail({kind:'employee',id:e.id})}>Open employee records</LinkButton>],['Qualification',()=> <Badge>Configuration required</Badge>],['Decision',()=> 'Chairman review after all gates are configured']
     ]}/><div className="inset"><p>Proposed starting gates from the draft: completion &gt;90%, on-time &gt;90%, revision &lt;10%, attendance &gt;95%, plus a minimum task count. These are not approved company targets.</p><p>Three consecutive qualifying months would create a Chairman review item with its evidence pack. No sample employee is declared eligible without attendance and target data.</p></div></Panel>;
     case 'access':return <><Panel title="Accounts and scoped mandates">{accessTable()}</Panel><Panel title="Account workflow"><div className="inset"><p>Requested → authorised mandate → account provisioned → role and scope checked → periodic review. Revocation ends sessions and records the reason. Admin maintains records; Super Admin reviews privileged changes.</p><Button onClick={()=>{setView('requests');setRequestType('Access change')}}>Create access request</Button></div></Panel></>;
     case 'configuration':return <><Panel title="Versioned system rules" subtitle="Demonstration values only; changes affect this preview.">{configView()}</Panel><Panel title="Decisions still needed"><div className="check-list">{['Performance targets and recognition minimum sample','Holiday calendar and grace periods','Critical severity as a separate risk level','Attendance, location and evidence retention periods','Allowed report recipients and export retention','Risk severity / business-impact mapping','Privacy and HR review of work-location processing'].map(s=><p key={s}><HelpCircle size={17}/>{s} · Not set</p>)}</div></Panel></>;
     case 'audit':return <Panel title="Audit and decision history" subtitle="Append-only in the interface. This local demo is not a tamper-proof audit store.">{auditTable()}</Panel>;
     case 'system':return systemView();
     case 'messages':return <div className="grid two wide-left"><Panel title="Conversations linked to work">{messageList()}</Panel><Panel title="Write a message"><div className="inset"><Field label="Recipient"><select value={recipient} onChange={e=>setRecipient(e.target.value)}>{employees.filter(e=>e.id!==role.employee).map(e=><option key={e.id} value={e.id}>{e.name}</option>)}</select></Field><Field label="Work reference"><select value={requestSource} onChange={e=>setRequestSource(e.target.value)}><option value="">Select linked task</option>{work.map(t=><option key={t.id}>{t.id}</option>)}</select></Field><Field label="Message"><textarea value={note} onChange={e=>setNote(e.target.value)}/></Field><Button primary icon={Send} disabled={!note.trim()||!requestSource} onClick={()=>{update(d=>d.messages.push({id:'MSG-'+Date.now(),from:role.employee,to:[recipient],task:requestSource,text:note,at:'13 Oct, 15:30'}),'Message added',requestSource);setNote('');notify('Message saved. Open the recipient’s demo to read it.')}}>Send demo message</Button></div></Panel></div>;
     case 'notifications':return <><Panel title="Notifications and reminders" action={<Button onClick={()=>update(d=>{d.read=[...new Set([...d.read,...risks.map(r=>r.id)])]})}>Mark all read</Button>}>{risks.map(r=><div className="attention-row" key={r.id}><Bell size={18}/><div><strong>{r.title}</strong><small>{r.source} · {data.read.includes(r.id)?'Read':'Unread'} · In-app delivery</small></div><Button onClick={()=>{update(d=>d.read.push(r.id));setDetail({kind:'risk',risk:r})}}>Open</Button></div>)}{!risks.length&&<Empty title="You are up to date" text="No task reminders are active in your scope."/>}</Panel>{announcementPanel()}</>;
     case 'reports':return reports();
     case 'profile':return <div className="grid two"><Panel title="Profile and role resolution"><div className="inset"><div className="employee-button"><Avatar name={me.name}/><div><h3>{me.name}</h3><p>{me.id} · {role.label}</p></div></div><dl className="details"><div><dt>Team / branch</dt><dd>{me.team} / {me.branch}</dd></div><div><dt>Session location</dt><dd>{data.attendance.find(a=>a.employee===me.id)?.location} · simulated check-in</dd></div><div><dt>Active role scope</dt><dd>{teamRole?'Assigned organisation / team scope':'Own work plus explicit service mandates'}</dd></div><div><dt>Role switch rule</dt><dd>Resolve allowed roles and refresh permissions from the backend on every switch.</dd></div></dl><p className="muted">The preview selector changes personas. It is not a real sign-in or an authorisation control.</p><Button onClick={()=>setDetail({kind:'security'})}>Password change design</Button></div></Panel><Panel title="Active sessions" subtitle="Simulated sessions; no production account is connected.">{data.sessions.map(s=><div className="attention-row" key={s.id}><UserRound size={18}/><div><strong>{s.device}</strong><small>{s.active?'Active':'Ended'}</small></div><Button disabled={!s.active||s.id==='SES-01'} onClick={()=>{update(d=>{d.sessions.find(x=>x.id===s.id).active=false},'Demo session ended',s.id);notify('Other demo session ended.')}}>End session</Button></div>)}<div className="inset"><h3>Login outcomes</h3><p>Invalid credentials → stay on login with a generic error. No role → support route. One role → workspace. Multiple roles → allowed-role choice. Unknown location → tag the session and continue.</p><a href="index.html" className="button">Open role-routing preview</a></div></Panel></div>;
     default:return null;
     }}
     function taskDrawer(t){const owner=t.owner===role.employee;const reviewer=canReview&&!owner;const required=t.evidence.filter(e=>e.required&&e.status!=='Superseded');const complete=required.length>=2&&required.every(e=>['Submitted','Accepted'].includes(e.status));const accepted=required.length>=2&&required.every(e=>e.status==='Accepted');const change=(action,fn,reason=note)=>{update(d=>{const task=d.tasks.find(x=>x.id===t.id);fn(task);task.history.push({at:ASOF,actor:role.employee,action,detail:reason||action});task.lastActivity=ASOF},action,t.id,reason);setNote('');notify(action+' saved.');};return <>
     <div className="drawer-meta"><Badge>{t.state}</Badge><span>{t.id} · {t.entity}</span><Badge>{t.priority}</Badge></div><dl className="details"><div><dt>Owner</dt><dd>{person(t.owner)}</dd></div><div><dt>Original due</dt><dd>{niceDate(t.originalDue)}</dd></div><div><dt>Approved due</dt><dd>{niceDate(t.due)}</dd></div><div><dt>First valid submission</dt><dd>{niceDate(t.firstSubmitted)}</dd></div><div><dt>Active effort / estimate</dt><dd>{t.effort} / {t.estimate} h</dd></div><div><dt>Elapsed time</dt><dd>{Math.max(0,Math.round((new Date(ASOF)-new Date(t.created))/86400000))} calendar days · separate from effort</dd></div><div><dt>Context</dt><dd>{t.exclusion||'No approved exclusion'}{t.blocker&&<small>{t.blocker}</small>}</dd></div></dl>
     <h3>Required evidence</h3><p className="muted">Submit only when complete. Close only after an independent reviewer accepts every required item.</p>{t.evidence.map((e,i)=><div className="evidence-item" key={e.id+'-'+i}><div><strong>{e.name}</strong><small>{e.type} · v{e.version} · {e.id}</small></div><Badge>{e.status}</Badge><p>{e.reason}</p><small>Submitted by {person(e.submitter)} · {e.reviewer?'Reviewed by '+person(e.reviewer):'No review yet'}</small>{owner&&['Missing','Rejected','Superseded'].includes(e.status)&&active(t)&&<Button onClick={()=>change('Evidence version added',task=>{const old=task.evidence[i];old.required=false;if(old.status!=='Rejected')old.status='Superseded';task.evidence.push({...old,id:old.id+'v2',required:true,version:String(Number(old.version)+1),status:'Submitted',time:ASOF,reason:'Demo evidence reference supplied; not a real upload.',reviewer:null});},'Versioned sample reference attached')}>Attach sample replacement</Button>}{reviewer&&e.required&&e.status==='Submitted'&&['Waiting for Review','Under Review'].includes(t.state)&&<div className="actions"><Button onClick={()=>change('Evidence accepted',task=>{task.evidence[i].status='Accepted';task.evidence[i].reviewer=role.employee;task.evidence[i].reason=note.trim()||'Checked sample reference against the required checklist.';task.state='Under Review'})}>Accept item</Button><Button disabled={!note.trim()} onClick={()=>change('Evidence rejected',task=>{task.evidence[i].status='Rejected';task.evidence[i].reviewer=role.employee;task.evidence[i].reason=note;task.state='Revision Required';task.revisionCount++})}>Reject with reason</Button></div>}</div>)}
     {active(t)&&<><h3>Work activity and decisions</h3><Field label="Note / decision reason"><textarea value={note} onChange={e=>setNote(e.target.value)} placeholder="Add context, a work update or a decision reason."/></Field><div className="actions">{(owner||reviewer)&&<Button disabled={!note.trim()} onClick={()=>change('Work note added',()=>{})}>Add note</Button>}{owner&&t.state==='Assigned'&&<Button primary onClick={()=>change('Task started',task=>{task.state='In Progress'})}>Start work</Button>}{owner&&['In Progress','Revision Required'].includes(t.state)&&<Button primary disabled={!complete} onClick={()=>change('Submitted for review',task=>{task.state='Waiting for Review';if(!task.firstSubmitted)task.firstSubmitted=ASOF})}>Submit for review</Button>}{reviewer&&['Waiting for Review','Under Review'].includes(t.state)&&<Button primary disabled={!accepted} onClick={()=>change('Task closed',task=>{task.state='Closed';task.closedAt=ASOF})}>Close accepted task</Button>}</div>{owner&&!complete&&<p className="helper">Submission is unavailable until every required item has a current submitted version.</p>}{reviewer&&<details className="advanced"><summary>Allocation and authorised changes</summary><Field label="New owner"><select value={recipient} onChange={e=>setRecipient(e.target.value)}>{directory.filter(e=>e.id!==t.owner).map(e=><option key={e.id} value={e.id}>{e.name}</option>)}</select></Field><div className="actions"><Button disabled={!note.trim()||recipient===t.owner} onClick={()=>change('Transferred',task=>{task.history.push({at:ASOF,actor:role.employee,action:'Ownership snapshot',detail:`${person(task.owner)} → ${person(recipient)}.     Add: C:\Users\ciril\iots-app\frontend\dasboards\README.md
    # CIRIL IOTS dashboard preview
    
    This folder contains **ten separate, self-contained React HTML workspaces**, plus a role-routing preview. Open **index.html** to start. React, Inter fonts, Lucide icons, CSS, the CIRIL logo and the sample data are embedded in each HTML file. Internet access is not required to view them.
    
    ## Open the connected preview
    
    Double-click any HTML file to inspect its role. For reliable shared changes across roles, serve the folder from one local address:
    
    ```powershell
    cd C:\Users\ciril\iots-app\frontend\dasboards
    npm run serve
    ```
    
    Open http://127.0.0.1:4178/. The preview server binds only to this computer. Browser storage under this address connects all workspaces. File URLs may use separate storage depending on the browser. The bottom **Demo controls → Reset demo** resets this prototype’s changes only.
    
    ## Role files and primary purpose
    
    | File | Fictional employee | Main view |
    |---|---|---|
    | chairman.html | Arvind Mehta | Enterprise delivery, attention queue, royalty, data confidence, recognition |
    | general-manager.html | Kavita Rao | Detailed employee monitor, capacity, membership, governance, finance follow-through |
    | senior-manager.html | Sanjay Nair | Team capacity, cross-team delivery and transfer history |
    | lead-manager.html | Priya Sharma | Allocation, independent evidence review, requests and specific feedback |
    | executive.html | Rohan Iyer | Own priorities, evidence submission, work activity and attendance |
    | bde.html | Aditi Deshmukh | Prospect stages, contacts, outreach, meetings, dated follow-ups and CRM handoffs |
    | creatives.html | Neha Kulkarni | Design and social work, proofreading, review, publishing and proof |
    | admin.html | Farah Khan | Profiles, attendance corrections, accounts and announcements |
    | super-admin.html | Vikram Joshi | Privileged mandates, versioned rules, exports and audit |
    | it-analyst.html | Arjun Menon | Service health, CRM retries, incidents, deployments, backups and recovery |
    
    Each file includes its permitted prototype views for work, performance definitions, evidence, attendance, requests/issues, notifications, work-linked messages, reports and profile/security. Role-specific navigation exposes membership, royalty, governance, creative delivery or platform operations where relevant. Admin employee administration does not expose employee performance detail. Prototype permissions are display rules; the backend must enforce real scope and mandates.
    
    ## Try a complete workflow
    
    1. Open Executive → **Compare Bengaluru office proposals (T-1043)**. Submission starts disabled because one required evidence item is missing.
    2. **Attach sample replacement**, then **Submit for review**. A first-submission timestamp and transition are recorded; the task ID stays the same.
    3. Open Lead Manager. Find the same task in **Ready for your review**. Accept both current required items. **Close accepted task** becomes available only after both independent acceptances.
    4. Open General Manager → employee monitor → Rohan. The employee card uses the same changed work record.
    5. Open Deals & royalty → CRM-2601. The ledger explains the brokerage shares and royalty calculation; its internal work links use the same IDs.
    
    Other working controls include light/dark theme, period selection and matching-cutoff comparisons, search, record filters, column sorting, pagination, detail drawers, work notes and sample effort entries, replacement evidence versions, transfer/extension/cancellation with a reason, feedback, requests and decisions, membership next steps, work-linked messages, notification read state, checkout/break controls, incident resolution, configuration versions and ending a simulated session.
    
    The report builder combines period, employee, manager, team, role, department, branch, priority, task state, request, attendance and risk filters. **Excel** creates a real `.xlsx` of scoped matching records. **Appraisal template** adds a review sheet. **PDF** uses the browser’s print / Save as PDF dialog. **Dashboard** retains the filtered preview. **Authorised email** records a simulated delivery job; it does not send email. Report jobs are recorded in the local audit history.
    
    ## Sample records and measurement rules
    
    - Twelve fictional Indian employees, 194 connected task records, historical attendance, four fictional CRM requirements, four fictional membership prospects, review evidence, requests, issues, messages and configuration records.
    - Snapshot: **13 October 2026, 15:30 IST**. CRM sample snapshot: **15:20 IST**. Fixed dates keep review reproducible.
    - Completion uses tasks due in the selected period up to the cutoff. On-time uses the first valid submission against both original and approved due dates. Future due dates do not enter the current completion cohort.
    - Cancelled work and approved leave/external-blocker exclusions remain visible with their context; eligible ratios exclude them. Zero denominator is **N/A**. Fewer than five observations display counts. Targets remain **Target not configured**.
    - Performance detail includes first-time acceptance, overdue rate/age, update compliance, planned utilisation, attendance, punctuality, median/p90 review duration, request response, blocker resolution, effort and elapsed duration. Definitions and source information are available with every measure.
    - The historical attendance and review calculations use an explicitly illustrative **Mon–Fri 09:00–18:00 IST calendar with no holidays**. This is a preview configuration, not an established CIRIL rule. Production calendars, grace periods, targets and retention periods require configuration.
    - Counts without sufficient source timestamps show N/A. Effort aggregates in the preview are labelled; production must use dated effort entries. Telemetry in the IT panels is labelled illustrative and is not connected to real monitoring.
    - Task state changes are explicit. Adding notes or effort does not submit or close work. Reassignments retain the ID and original deadline; extension records retain the original date and audit reason. Evidence rejection/supersession remains visible.
    - CRM amounts are read-only. CIRIL royalty is **7.5% of each party’s brokerage share** from the supplied specification. The **30/70 split is a sample agreement only**. CRM-2601: ₹12,00,000 brokerage → ₹27,000 giver royalty + ₹63,000 receiver royalty; ₹27,000 verified collected → ₹63,000 outstanding. These amounts and payment references are fictional.
    - Recognition demonstrates the configuration-required state. No employee is declared qualified or ranked without the required targets, attendance evidence, minimum task count and scoring weights.
    
    ## Research and source boundaries
    
    Local source authority, in priority order:
    
    1. `iots-app/documentation/plan/tracking_draft_chatGPT.docx`: measurement definitions, fair denominators, role workspaces, evidence rules, shared services and engineering requirements.
    2. `iots-app/documentation/iots-system.drawio`: login/routing, availability, task/request/issue outcomes, domain workflows and reports.
    3. `Ai-Designed Flowchart/essentials/inputs/claude_version.docx`: member alliance operations, cross-city requirements, proposals, agreements, coordination and royalty follow-up. Earlier role splits and unconfirmed targets in this source do not override the latest ten-role draft.
    4. Existing React frontend: charcoal `#202830`, warm gold `#C09860`, off-white surfaces, Inter and the CIRIL logo.
    5. `Member-Passwords-List.xlsx`: **only columns B (zone), C (location) and D (member office)** were decoded into `src/members-source.json`. No password, login ID, email, phone or credential values were used. Directory casing is normalised for display; source spellings are preserved.
    
    Public sources checked for company context:
    
    - [CIRIL’s description of its collaborative commercial real-estate network and services](https://www.ciril.in/about-ciril-real-estate-consultancy).
    - [CIRIL’s membership-network information](https://www.ciril.in/join-ciril-real-estate-network).
    - [CIRIL’s member location directory](https://www.ciril.in/commercial-real-estate-location-directory).
    
    The design reflects member firms receiving cross-city requirements, HQ coordinating owners and handoffs, local proposals progressing to negotiation/agreements, and finance verification following the concluded transaction. Public materials establish the network context; internal approval authority, employee targets, financial shares and implementation details come from the supplied internal specification, not from assumptions about the public website.
    
    ## Integration boundary
    
    This delivery is a **design prototype**, not a deployed IOTS system. It does not authenticate users, scan/upload actual files, collect passwords, send email, perform payments or track a device location. All writes are local browser demo changes. Every role HTML contains the full fictional seed so it can run independently; role selection is a persona preview, not a security boundary.
    
    For production React 19 + Express 5 integration, replace `getData`, `update`, `scopeIds` and browser storage with `/api/v1` contracts. The server must resolve active roles, permissions, assigned employee/entity scope and decision mandates; reject self-review; validate transition/evidence gates; preserve append-only activity/decisions and deadline history; provide metric definitions and data-as-of timestamps; and authorize each evidence/report download. Use the existing login only after these contracts are connected.
    
    Suggested panel endpoints: `/api/v1/me/workspaces`, `/dashboard`, `/tasks`, `/tasks/:id/activity`, `/tasks/:id/transitions`, `/evidence`, `/employees/:id/monitor`, `/attendance`, `/requests`, `/issues`, `/members`, `/membership-prospects`, `/crm/deals`, `/creative-deliveries`, `/messages`, `/notifications`, `/reports/jobs`, `/sessions`, `/configuration/versions`, `/audit` and `/operations/health`. These are proposed integration contracts, not implemented APIs.
    
    ## Rebuild and verification
    
    ```powershell
    npm install
    npm run build
    npm run serve
    ```
    
    `src/App.jsx` holds the shared React views, `src/data.js` the seeded domain records and measurement helpers, and `src/style.css` the design system. `build.mjs` emits all eleven HTML files. Do not hand-edit the generated HTML before rebuilding.
    
    `npm test` checks metric edge cases and royalty arithmetic, source links, independent review, all role navigation, desktop/mobile overflow, cross-role submission/closure, scoped Excel export, recovery states and drawer dismissal. The local test uses Microsoft Edge at the standard Windows installation path. Screenshots, automated accessibility results and the final design review are stored in `.impeccable/review/`. Automated checks support review; they do not replace usability testing with CIRIL employees.

    Routing:
    
    - **No argument:** read [routing.md](reference/routing.md) and present its context-aware menu; never auto-run a command.
    - **Explicit or clearly implied request to run a command:** load its reference (native variant on native platforms) and follow it. Ask once if two commands fit.
    - **Workflow or command-selection question:** read [Workflow questions](reference/routing.md#workflow-questions).
    - **Otherwise:** treat the request as general design work. Missing PRODUCT.md routes a new surface or replacement world through init, then new-work; a narrow refinement of existing code proceeds on the incumbent implementation as `impeccable context` directs, offering init afterward rather than blocking on it.
    - `teach` aliases `init`. `craft` is a deprecated alias for ordinary new-work and adds nothing. `shape` owns task discovery, then enters new-work only for visual-world and surface-concept decisions.
    
    After init writes PRODUCT.md, resume without rerunning `impeccable context`; init loads the native platform reference itself when the platform it recorded is `ios`, `android`, or `adaptive`.
    
    **Pin / Unpin:** `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable pin <pin|unpin> <command>` creates or removes a standalone `$<command>` shortcut. Report the script's result concisely; relay stderr verbatim on error.
    
    **Hooks:** `$impeccable hooks <on|off|status|ignore-rule|ignore-file|ignore-value|reset>` manages the design detector hook for this project (auto-runs the detector after UI file edits and surfaces findings). Load [reference/hooks.md](reference/hooks.md) when the user invokes it with any argument.
    
    **Doctor:** `$impeccable doctor` reports and repairs drift between this project's Impeccable artifacts (PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md and its sidecar, config, surface briefs, the hook) and what this version reads. Load [reference/doctor.md](reference/doctor.md) when the user invokes it, or when they ask what is out of date, stale, or needs refreshing. A `CONTEXT_STALE` directive in Setup's output is the cheap subset of the same report; act on it there per its own instructions rather than running doctor unasked.
    
    **Never repair drift as a side effect of a design task.** A `CONTEXT_STALE` finding is reported, not acted on, unless the user asks. The one exception is a finding marked `auto`, which the next write to that file performs anyway.

    # CIRIL IOTS dashboard design system
    
    This prototype extends the existing CIRIL frontend rather than introducing a new visual identity. It is designed for people who spend a workday reviewing registers, approvals, tasks and operational exceptions.
    
    ## Visual decisions
    
    - **Typography:** Inter at a compact fixed product scale. Main headings are 28px desktop / 25px mobile; compact labels, table metadata and audit context use 10–12px. Numbers use tabular figures.
    - **Colour:** charcoal `#202830` is the navigation and dark-mode foundation; warm gold `#C09860` marks current context and primary actions; warm off-white `#F6F5F2` and white surfaces support long sessions. Semantic green, amber and red express accepted/healthy, attention and exception states with text labels.
    - **Surfaces:** 12px panels use a one-pixel border, no decorative gradients or shadow-heavy cards. Tables and lists carry most content; panels group a work question rather than acting as generic visual tiles.
    - **Layout:** a fixed 235px desktop navigation and compact top bar frame a maximum 1720px content area. Role home pages begin with matched-period measures and lead into role-specific operational records. At 760px the nav becomes a drawer, metrics become two columns, and tables retain horizontal scroll with a visible scroll cue.
    - **Interaction:** standard controls use 6px corners, visible gold focus rings, keyboard-accessible native inputs and Radix detail dialogs. Motion is limited to a short drawer reveal and respects reduced-motion preference.
    
    ## Reusable component rules
    
    `Panel` has a titled header, optional context/action and a contained register or decision surface. `Table` supports sort, pagination and a labelled horizontal region; its mobile cue tells users when columns continue off screen. `Badge` always combines colour with status text. `Metric` links to its numerator, denominator, scope, source, cutoff and definition. The detail drawer is for work records, decisions and evidence history rather than decorative expansion.
    
    Use the dark sidebar and gold selected navigation state consistently. Do not use the gold colour as decoration or convey a decision by colour alone. Keep work state, evidence state and risk state visibly separate.
    
    ## Content and trust rules
    
    Every dashboard says the data is a fictional prototype and identifies its data-as-of time. Values describe the sample calendar, source and configuration state. “Target not configured”, “N/A” and low-sample counts are intentional states. The UI must not infer authorization from a display role; the production backend resolves scope and mandates. Location is an explicit attendance-event tag only. The member directory contains firm/city/zone fields only.
    
    ## Accessibility and responsive requirements
    
    Maintain semantic headings, labelled controls, keyboard focus, escape-to-close detail dialogs, text alternatives for compact charts and accessible contrast in both themes. At narrow widths, preserve task information with scrollable tables and the visible cue; do not silently remove task deadlines, evidence or employee fields. Empty, loading, error and partial-data previews should state both the condition and recovery action.

    $ Get-Content -LiteralPath 'C:\Users\ciril\.agents\skills\impeccable\reference\animate.md'; Get-Content -LiteralPath 'C:\Users\ciril\.agents\skills\impeccable\reference\craft-floor.md'
    > **Additional context needed**: performance constraints.
    
    Use motion to explain state, relationship, and hierarchy, or to create one authored moment the surface has earned. Decoration without purpose is animation debt.
    
    ---
    
    ## Visitor mode
    
    - **Persuade + Experience:** motion may carry the voice. Prefer one rehearsed focal sequence to repeated section reveals.
    - **Operate + Read:** motion serves feedback, state, and continuity. Keep routine transitions fast and do not make users wait through page-load choreography.
    - **Native (`ios` / `android` / `adaptive`):** follow the Motion section of [ios.md](ios.md) or [android.md](android.md), including the platform's Reduce Motion behavior. Do not apply the web tooling below.
    
    ## Find the job
    
    Inspect the existing motion language, interaction states, target devices, and performance budget. Find only the places where motion would:
    
    - acknowledge an action;
    - make a state change or spatial relationship legible;
    - preserve continuity through navigation or layout change;
    - direct attention at a meaningful moment;
    - embody the selected visual world.
    
    Ask only when a material constraint cannot be inferred. Do not animate a static area merely because it exists.
    
    ## Set the motion thesis
    
    Write a short plan before implementation:
    
    - **Focal moment:** the one sequence or interaction that deserves authorship, if any.
    - **Continuity:** the state, layout, or navigation changes that need explanation.
    - **Feedback:** the controls and outcomes that need acknowledgment.
    - **Budget:** which effects may be expensive and how often they run.
    
    The focal moment must come from this product and surface concept. A generic fade-and-rise, hover lift, parallax layer, or scroll reveal is not a thesis.
    
    ## Choose material by meaning
    
    Transform and opacity are reliable foundations, not the entire palette. Choose properties for what the transition communicates:
    
    - **Continuity and relationship:** shared-element motion, FLIP-style transforms, view transitions, or deliberate spatial movement.
    - **Focus and depth:** bounded blur, filter, backdrop, light, or shadow changes.
    - **Reveal and composition:** masks, clip paths, cropping, or controlled occlusion.
    - **Material and energy:** color, gradient position, texture, distortion, or shader effects when the world and runtime support them.
    - **State and feedback:** the smallest change that makes cause and result unmistakable.
    
    Do not stack techniques for spectacle. One strong material idea, carried through the focal sequence and quiet supporting states, is usually enough.
    
    Sibling stagger is appropriate when a list appears as a list. Cap the total delay, and never reinterpret every scrolled section as a staggered list.
    
    ## Timing and easing
    
    Timing should express distance and consequence:
    
    | Duration | Typical use |
    |---|---|
    | 100â€“150 ms | immediate feedback |
    | 150â€“300 ms | routine state change |
    | 300â€“500 ms | layout, overlay, or view transition |
    | 500â€“800 ms | a deliberately authored focal entrance |
    
    Exit faster than entrance. Use natural deceleration such as `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` for confident arrivals; do not use bounce or elastic curves by reflex. Long feedback feels like latency.
    
    ## Implement to the runtime
    
    - Use CSS transitions and keyframes for declarative state and bounded sequences.
    - Use Web Animations API or the project's existing motion library for interruption, sequencing, and dynamic values.
    - Use View Transitions or shared-element techniques when continuity across states is the point.
    - Use scroll-driven motion only when the scroll relationship itself carries meaning, with a robust fallback.
    - Do not add a dependency for an effect the existing stack can express cleanly.
    
    Keep content visible in the default state so failed scripts do not hide the page. Avoid casually animating layout-driving properties such as `width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, and margins; use FLIP, transforms, or grid techniques when appropriate. Bound blur, filter, shadow, canvas, and shader work to isolated regions. Apply `will-change` only during known animation. Measure on target viewports and devices rather than assuming transform means fast.
    
    ## Accessibility and control
    
    Respect autoplay and sound preferences. Any nonessential loop must stop when offscreen or hidden.
    
    Every web animation needs a `prefers-reduced-motion` path with an intentional alternative. Remove or reduce spatial movement while preserving opacity, color, and state transitions that carry meaning. Reduced motion means fewer and gentler animations, not disabling all motion; feedback that confirms an action should remain legible.
    
    ## Verify
    
    - The focal motion is specific to the selected world and surface.
    - Every supporting animation explains feedback, state, or relationship.
    - Interruption and repeated use behave correctly.
    - Desktop, mobile, and keyboard paths remain usable.
    - The `prefers-reduced-motion` path reduces movement without erasing meaningful feedback or state changes.
    - Expensive effects stay smooth on the target device.
    - Removing an animation would lose meaning or authored character, not merely decoration.
    
    When motion earns its place, hand off to `$impeccable polish` for the final pass.
    # Craft floor
    
    Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.
    
    ## Verify
    
    Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in the batched inspection rounds, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.
    
    - **Contrast:** body and placeholder text â‰¥4.5:1, large text â‰¥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
    - **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
    - **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
    - **Type:** body measure 65â€“75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
    - **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
    - **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
    - **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, and the numerals in tabular data all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system. Theme them from the palette. This is the cheapest signal that a page was built rather than assembled, and the one models skip most reliably.
    - **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
    - **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.
    
    ## Refuse
    
    These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.
    
    Page scaffolds:
    
    - Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
    - The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
    - A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
    - Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
    - A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.
    
    Surface habits:
    
    - Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
    - Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
    - A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
    - Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
    - Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
    - Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
    - A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
    - Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
    - Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
    - Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.
    
    - Tracking stops at -0.04em. -0.02 to -0.03em usually reads better.
    - Declare elevation once, border or shadow. A 1px border under a wide soft shadow is the ghost card. Card radii stay at 12â€“16px; pills are for small controls.
    - Real illustration or none. Sketch-style SVG scenes, `loose-sketch` / `doodle` class names, and `feTurbulence` grain read as amateur. This bans SVG imitating pictures, never SVG doing geometry: crisp vector shapes, diagrams, animated linework, and shader-driven effects remain first-class media. A shaded, perspectived, or figure-bearing illustration is a picture even in line-art style; geometry means shapes a session can specify exactly.
    - Backgrounds are surfaces, textured only from the subject's world. `repeating-linear-gradient` stripes and two-axis grid overlays need an actual canvas, map, blueprint, or measuring tool under them.
    - Claims and configuration come from supplied truth; label illustrative values honestly. Naming a concept and then ironizing it is not a claim.
    
    The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.

    # Design System: CIRIL IOTS Dashboard System
    
    ## Overview
    
    **Creative North Star: "The Evidence Ledger"**
    
    CIRIL IOTS is a light-first operational system for reading, reviewing, and acting on dense work records. It extends the established CIRIL frontend with Inter, charcoal navigation, warm gold emphasis, warm white surfaces, and plain, inspectable structure. Role-specific dashboards vary the work in view while keeping the shell, controls, registers, and detail behavior consistent.
    
    **Key Characteristics:**
    - Stable charcoal left navigation and compact utility top bar.
    - Dense, readable panels and scrollable registers for operational review.
    - Warm gold marks selection and action; semantic tones state outcome and risk.
    - Responsive layouts preserve work context rather than simplifying records away.
    
    ## Colors
    
    Warm paper-like neutrals carry long daytime sessions; charcoal establishes orientation and gold signals the work that needs attention.
    
    ### Primary
    - **CIRIL Warm Gold:** Used for primary actions, selected navigation, timeline markers, and measured emphasis.
    
    ### Neutral
    - **Charcoal Frame:** The fixed sidebar and toast surface.
    - **Warm Canvas and White Surface:** The page ground and working panels.
    - **Quiet Ink and Muted Register Text:** The reading hierarchy for dense records.
    - **Fine Divider:** Separates rows and surface regions without visual weight.
    
    ### Named Rules
    **The Gold Is a Signal Rule.** Gold identifies selection, action, and important progress; it is not a general fill for every panel.
    
    ## Typography
    
    **Display Font:** Inter, sans-serif
    
    **Body Font:** Inter, sans-serif
    
    **Character:** Compact, sober, and highly legible. The type scale lets titles establish context while 10–13px labels and records support close operational scanning.
    
    ### Hierarchy
    - **Display:** Used for page titles and landing introduction.
    - **Headline:** Used in drawers and prominent record detail.
    - **Title:** Used for panel headings and role tiles.
    - **Body:** Used for explanatory and record content, with paragraphs limited to readable measures.
    - **Label:** Used for controls, table headers, utility metadata, and badges.
    
    ### Named Rules
    **The Register-First Rule.** Use hierarchy to clarify work and evidence; do not introduce decorative display treatments into register surfaces.
    
    ## Layout
    
    The desktop shell fixes a 235px left sidebar beside the content area. The top bar is 70px and main work has a 32px desktop inset, constrained to 1720px. Panels use 20px gaps and interiors; summary strips show four measures, then two at 1050px. At 760px the sidebar becomes an off-canvas 260px drawer, the top bar becomes 60px, content uses 16px insets, grids stack, and tables remain horizontally scrollable with a visible scroll cue.
    
    ## Elevation & Depth
    
    The system is flat by default. Borders and warm tonal shifts define resting surfaces. A dim overlay and soft directional shadow establish the detail drawer; the charcoal toast receives a compact ambient lift. Motion is brief: background state changes use 0.15s, and drawers reveal over 0.18s; reduced-motion disables both.
    
    ### Named Rules
    **The Work Surface Rule.** Panels are separated by borders and spacing; elevation is reserved for temporary layers that sit above active work.
    
    ## Shapes
    
    Controls use gently rounded 6px corners, badges use 4px, notices and toast use 8px, and panels use 12px. Avatars and status dots are circular. Borders are thin and neutral; no heavy outlines or ornamental silhouettes appear.
    
    ## Components
    
    ### Buttons
    - **Shape:** Compact rounded control (6px), normally 36px high with 8px by 12px padding.
    - **Primary:** Warm gold with charcoal text.
    - **Default:** White surface with a fine border; hover changes to the subtle surface.
    - **Focus:** A visible 2px focus outline using the focus color.
    
    ### Badges
    - **Style:** Compact 11px labels with 4px corners and 4px by 7px padding.
    - **State:** Green success, amber warning, red danger, and neutral muted states always pair color with text.
    
    ### Cards / Containers
    - **Corner Style:** 12px.
    - **Background:** White surface with a thin neutral border.
    - **Internal Padding:** Panel headings use 19–20px and bodies continue the same rhythm.
    
    ### Inputs / Fields
    - **Style:** White surface, 1px divider border, 6px corners, and a 38px minimum height.
    - **Focus:** 2px visible focus outline; search fields show the same treatment on focus within.
    
    ### Navigation
    - **Style:** A fixed charcoal sidebar with compact 12px rows and 6px corners, paired with a quiet utility top bar.
    - **State:** Hover lightens the row; selected entries use a warm dark field with gold text and icon. Mobile navigation moves off canvas and uses a backdrop and close control.
    
    ### Tables / Registers
    - **Style:** Tabular numbers, muted 10px headers, 11px body rows, subtle header fill, and thin row dividers.
    - **Behavior:** Rows receive a subtle hover surface. Columns sort through labeled controls; wide tables scroll horizontally and show a mobile scroll cue.
    
    ### Detail Drawer
    - **Style:** A right-side white working layer up to 680px wide, with a dim overlay and one directional shadow.
    - **Behavior:** It carries record detail above the register and becomes full-width on small screens.
    
    ## Do's and Don'ts
    
    ### Do:
    - **Do** retain the stable sidebar, utility bar, page title, summary strip, and register sequence for role dashboards.
    - **Do** use semantic badge text with green, amber, red, or neutral treatment for status.
    - **Do** keep mobile tables scrollable and communicate that additional columns are available.
    - **Do** preserve visible keyboard focus and respect reduced-motion preferences.
    
    ### Don't:
    - **Don't** use warm gold as a broad decorative background or as the only indicator of state.
    - **Don't** remove row dividers, scopes, or metadata from dense operational registers to make a dashboard look sparse.
    - **Don't** introduce heavy resting shadows or large rounded consumer-app cards into work surfaces.
    - **Don't** rely on hover alone for record status, actions, or table access.

    # Design System: CIRIL IOTS Dashboard System
    
    ## Overview
    
    **Creative North Star: "The Evidence Ledger"**
    
    CIRIL IOTS is a light-first operational system for reading, reviewing, and acting on dense work records. It extends the established CIRIL frontend with Inter, charcoal navigation, warm gold emphasis, warm white surfaces, and plain, inspectable structure. Role-specific dashboards vary the work in view while keeping the shell, controls, registers, and detail behavior consistent.
    
    **Key Characteristics:**
    - Stable charcoal left navigation and compact utility top bar.
    - Dense, readable panels and scrollable registers for operational review.
    - Warm gold marks selection and action; semantic tones state outcome and risk.
    - Responsive layouts preserve work context rather than simplifying records away.
    
    ## Colors
    
    Warm paper-like neutrals carry long daytime sessions; charcoal establishes orientation and gold signals the work that needs attention.
    
    ### Primary
    - **CIRIL Warm Gold:** Used for primary actions, selected navigation, timeline markers, and measured emphasis.
    
    ### Neutral
    - **Charcoal Frame:** The fixed sidebar and toast surface.
    - **Warm Canvas and White Surface:** The page ground and working panels.
    - **Quiet Ink and Muted Register Text:** The reading hierarchy for dense records.
    - **Fine Divider:** Separates rows and surface regions without visual weight.
    
    ### Named Rules
    **The Gold Is a Signal Rule.** Gold identifies selection, action, and important progress; it is not a general fill for every panel.
    
    ## Typography
    
    **Display Font:** Inter, sans-serif
    
    **Body Font:** Inter, sans-serif
    
    **Character:** Compact, sober, and highly legible. The type scale lets titles establish context while 10â€“13px labels and records support close operational scanning.
    
    ### Hierarchy
    - **Display:** Used for page titles and landing introduction.
    - **Headline:** Used in drawers and prominent record detail.
    - **Title:** Used for panel headings and role tiles.
    - **Body:** Used for explanatory and record content, with paragraphs limited to readable measures.
    - **Label:** Used for controls, table headers, utility metadata, and badges.
    
    ### Named Rules
    **The Register-First Rule.** Use hierarchy to clarify work and evidence; do not introduce decorative display treatments into register surfaces.
    
    ## Layout
    
    The desktop shell fixes a 235px left sidebar beside the content area. The top bar is 70px and main work has a 32px desktop inset, constrained to 1720px. Panels use 20px gaps and interiors; summary strips show four measures, then two at 1050px. At 760px the sidebar becomes an off-canvas 260px drawer, the top bar becomes 60px, content uses 16px insets, grids stack, and tables remain horizontally scrollable with a visible scroll cue.
    
    ## Elevation & Depth
    
    The system is flat by default. Borders and warm tonal shifts define resting surfaces. A dim overlay and soft directional shadow establish the detail drawer; the charcoal toast receives a compact ambient lift. Motion is brief: background state changes use 0.15s, and drawers reveal over 0.18s; reduced-motion disables both.
    
    ### Named Rules
    **The Work Surface Rule.** Panels are separated by borders and spacing; elevation is reserved for temporary layers that sit above active work.
    
    ## Shapes
    
    Controls use gently rounded 6px corners, badges use 4px, notices and toast use 8px, and panels use 12px. Avatars and status dots are circular. Borders are thin and neutral; no heavy outlines or ornamental silhouettes appear.
    
    ## Components
    
    ### Buttons
    - **Shape:** Compact rounded control (6px), normally 36px high with 8px by 12px padding.
    - **Primary:** Warm gold with charcoal text.
    - **Default:** White surface with a fine border; hover changes to the subtle surface.
    - **Focus:** A visible 2px focus outline using the focus color.
    
    ### Badges
    - **Style:** Compact 11px labels with 4px corners and 4px by 7px padding.
    - **State:** Green success, amber warning, red danger, and neutral muted states always pair color with text.
    
    ### Cards / Containers
    - **Corner Style:** 12px.
    - **Background:** White surface with a thin neutral border.
    - **Internal Padding:** Panel headings use 19â€“20px and bodies continue the same rhythm.
    
    ### Inputs / Fields
    - **Style:** White surface, 1px divider border, 6px corners, and a 38px minimum height.
    - **Focus:** 2px visible focus outline; search fields show the same treatment on focus within.
    
    ### Navigation
    - **Style:** A fixed charcoal sidebar with compact 12px rows and 6px corners, paired with a quiet utility top bar.
    - **State:** Hover lightens the row; selected entries use a warm dark field with gold text and icon. Mobile navigation moves off canvas and uses a backdrop and close control.
    
    ### Tables / Registers
    - **Style:** Tabular numbers, muted 10px headers, 11px body rows, subtle header fill, and thin row dividers.
    - **Behavior:** Rows receive a subtle hover surface. Columns sort through labeled controls; wide tables scroll horizontally and show a mobile scroll cue.
    
    ### Detail Drawer
    - **Style:** A right-side white working layer up to 680px wide, with a dim overlay and one directional shadow.
    - **Behavior:** It carries record detail above the register and becomes full-width on small screens.
    
    ## Do's and Don'ts
    
    ### Do:
    - **Do** retain the stable sidebar, utility bar, page title, summary strip, and register sequence for role dashboards.
    - **Do** use semantic badge text with green, amber, red, or neutral treatment for status.
    - **Do** keep mobile tables scrollable and communicate that additional columns are available.
    - **Do** preserve visible keyboard focus and respect reduced-motion preferences.
    
    ### Don't:
    - **Don't** use warm gold as a broad decorative background or as the only indicator of state.
    - **Don't** remove row dividers, scopes, or metadata from dense operational registers to make a dashboard look sparse.
    - **Don't** introduce heavy resting shadows or large rounded consumer-app cards into work surfaces.
    - **Don't** rely on hover alone for record status, actions, or table access.

    # Design System: CIRIL IOTS Dashboard System
    
    ## Overview
    
    **Creative North Star: "The Evidence Ledger"**
    
    CIRIL IOTS is a light-first operational system for reading, reviewing, and acting on dense work records. It extends the established CIRIL frontend with Inter, charcoal navigation, warm gold emphasis, warm white surfaces, and plain, inspectable structure. Role-specific dashboards vary the work in view while keeping the shell, controls, registers, and detail behavior consistent.
    
    **Key Characteristics:**
    - Stable charcoal left navigation and compact utility top bar.
    - Dense, readable panels and scrollable registers for operational review.
    - Warm gold marks selection and action; semantic tones state outcome and risk.
    - Responsive layouts preserve work context rather than simplifying records away.
    
    ## Colors
    
    Warm paper-like neutrals carry long daytime sessions; charcoal establishes orientation and gold signals the work that needs attention.
    
    ### Primary
    - **CIRIL Warm Gold:** Used for primary actions, selected navigation, timeline markers, and measured emphasis.
    
    ### Neutral
    - **Charcoal Frame:** The fixed sidebar and toast surface.
    - **Warm Canvas and White Surface:** The page ground and working panels.
    - **Quiet Ink and Muted Register Text:** The reading hierarchy for dense records.
    - **Fine Divider:** Separates rows and surface regions without visual weight.
    
    ### Named Rules
    **The Gold Is a Signal Rule.** Gold identifies selection, action, and important progress; it is not a general fill for every panel.
    
    ## Typography
    
    **Display Font:** Inter, sans-serif
    
    **Body Font:** Inter, sans-serif
    
    **Character:** Compact, sober, and highly legible. The type scale lets titles establish context while 10–13px labels and records support close operational scanning.
    
    ### Hierarchy
    - **Display:** Used for page titles and landing introduction.
    - **Headline:** Used in drawers and prominent record detail.
    - **Title:** Used for panel headings and role tiles.
    - **Body:** Used for explanatory and record content, with paragraphs limited to readable measures.
    - **Label:** Used for controls, table headers, utility metadata, and badges.
    
    ### Named Rules
    **The Register-First Rule.** Use hierarchy to clarify work and evidence; do not introduce decorative display treatments into register surfaces.
    
    ## Layout
    
    The desktop shell fixes a 235px left sidebar beside the content area. The top bar is 70px and main work has a 32px desktop inset, constrained to 1720px. Panels use 20px gaps and interiors; summary strips show four measures, then two at 1050px. At 760px the sidebar becomes an off-canvas 260px drawer, the top bar becomes 60px, content uses 16px insets, grids stack, and tables remain horizontally scrollable with a visible scroll cue.
    
    ## Elevation & Depth
    
    The system is flat by default. Borders and warm tonal shifts define resting surfaces. A dim overlay and soft directional shadow establish the detail drawer; the charcoal toast receives a compact ambient lift.
    
    ### Named Rules
    **The Work Surface Rule.** Panels are separated by borders and spacing; elevation is reserved for temporary layers that sit above active work.
    
    ## Motion
    
    The first workspace load presents a skeleton for 950ms, or without delay when reduced motion is requested. It then runs one evidence-arrival sequence: summary strips, notes, grids, and panels rise into place with short staggered delays. This entrance state is cleared before any navigation view renders, so changing views never replays it.
    
    Buttons, icon controls, cards, role tiles, and actionable rows provide brief hover lift and press feedback. Segments and chart columns grow into their measured values; overlays fade in, drawers arrive from the right, and toasts enter from below. Desktop toasts are centred against the work surface; on mobile they span the 16px page inset and use a vertical arrival.
    
    **Reduced Motion:** `prefers-reduced-motion` disables visual animations and transitions. Actions, status changes, drawer access, and toast feedback remain immediate.
    
    ## Shapes
    
    Controls use gently rounded 6px corners, badges use 4px, notices and toast use 8px, and panels use 12px. Avatars and status dots are circular. Borders are thin and neutral; no heavy outlines or ornamental silhouettes appear.
    
    ## Components
    
    ### Buttons
    - **Shape:** Compact rounded control (6px), normally 36px high with 8px by 12px padding.
    - **Primary:** Warm gold with charcoal text.
    - **Default:** White surface with a fine border; hover changes to the subtle surface.
    - **Focus:** A visible 2px focus outline using the focus color.
    
    ### Badges
    - **Style:** Compact 11px labels with 4px corners and 4px by 7px padding.
    - **State:** Green success, amber warning, red danger, and neutral muted states always pair color with text.
    
    ### Cards / Containers
    - **Corner Style:** 12px.
    - **Background:** White surface with a thin neutral border.
    - **Internal Padding:** Panel headings use 19–20px and bodies continue the same rhythm.
    
    ### Inputs / Fields
    - **Style:** White surface, 1px divider border, 6px corners, and a 38px minimum height.
    - **Focus:** 2px visible focus outline; search fields show the same treatment on focus within.
    
    ### Navigation
    - **Style:** A fixed charcoal sidebar with compact 12px rows and 6px corners, paired with a quiet utility top bar.
    - **State:** Hover lightens the row; selected entries use a warm dark field with gold text and icon. Mobile navigation moves off canvas and uses a backdrop and close control.
    
    ### Tables / Registers
    - **Style:** Tabular numbers, muted 10px headers, 11px body rows, subtle header fill, and thin row dividers.
    - **Behavior:** Rows receive a subtle hover surface. Columns sort through labeled controls; wide tables scroll horizontally and show a mobile scroll cue.
    
    ### Detail Drawer
    - **Style:** A right-side white working layer up to 680px wide, with a dim overlay and one directional shadow.
    - **Behavior:** It carries record detail above the register and becomes full-width on small screens.
    
    ## Do's and Don'ts
    
    ### Do:
    - **Do** retain the stable sidebar, utility bar, page title, summary strip, and register sequence for role dashboards.
    - **Do** use semantic badge text with green, amber, red, or neutral treatment for status.
    - **Do** keep mobile tables scrollable and communicate that additional columns are available.
    - **Do** preserve visible keyboard focus and respect reduced-motion preferences.
    
    ### Don't:
    - **Don't** use warm gold as a broad decorative background or as the only indicator of state.
    - **Don't** remove row dividers, scopes, or metadata from dense operational registers to make a dashboard look sparse.
    - **Don't** introduce heavy resting shadows or large rounded consumer-app cards into work surfaces.
    - **Don't** rely on hover alone for record status, actions, or table access.
